href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-8\" data-mw-group=\"lower-alpha\" id=\"mwKQ\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwKg\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwKw\">[</span>a<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwLA\">]</span></span></a></sup> is the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Capital_of_Germany\" title=\"Capital of Germany\" id=\"mwLQ\">capital</a> and <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./List_of_cities_in_Germany_by_population\" title=\"List of cities in Germany by population\" id=\"mwLg\">largest city</a> of Germany. With 3.7 million inhabitants,<sup about=\"#mwt65\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-Destatis.Population_3-1\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{\"name\":\"Destatis.Population\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-Destatis.Population-3\" id=\"mwLw\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwMA\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwMQ\">[</span>3<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwMg\">]</span></span></a></sup> it has the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./List_of_cities_in_the_European_Union_by_population_within_city_limits\" title=\"List of cities in the European Union by population within city limits\" id=\"mwMw\">highest population</a> within its <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./City_limits\" title=\"City limits\" id=\"mwNA\">city limits</a> of any city in the European Union. The city is also one of the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./States_of_Germany\" title=\"States of Germany\" id=\"mwNQ\">states of Germany</a>, being the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./List_of_German_states_by_area\" title=\"List of German states by area\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwNg\">third-smallest state</a> in the country by area. Berlin is surrounded by the state of <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Brandenburg\" title=\"Brandenburg\" id=\"mwNw\">Brandenburg</a>, bordering Brandenburg's capital <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Potsdam\" title=\"Potsdam\" id=\"mwOA\">Potsdam</a> to the southwest. The urban area of Berlin has a population of 4.5 million, making it the second most populous in Germany after the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Ruhr\" title=\"Ruhr\" id=\"mwOQ\">Ruhr</a>.<sup about=\"#mwt66\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-UrbanAgglomerations_4-1\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{\"name\":\"UrbanAgglomerations\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-UrbanAgglomerations-4\" id=\"mwOg\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwOw\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwPA\">[</span>4<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwPQ\">]</span></span></a></sup> The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berlin/Brandenburg_Metropolitan_Region\" title=\"Berlin/Brandenburg Metropolitan Region\" id=\"mwPg\">Berlin-Brandenburg capital region</a> has around 6.2 million inhabitants and is Germany's <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Metropolitan_regions_in_Germany\" title=\"Metropolitan regions in Germany\" id=\"mwPw\">second-largest metropolitan region</a> after the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Rhine-Ruhr\" title=\"Rhine-Ruhr\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwQA\">Rhine-Ruhr</a> region,<sup about=\"#mwt69\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-9\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-9\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-9\" id=\"mwQQ\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwQg\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwQw\">[</span>8<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwRA\">]</span></span></a></sup> as well as the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./List_of_EU_metropolitan_areas_by_GDP\" title=\"List of EU metropolitan areas by GDP\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwRQ\">fifth-biggest metropolitan region by GDP</a> in the European Union.</p>\n\n<p id=\"mwRg\">Berlin was built along the banks of the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Spree_(river)\" title=\"Spree (river)\" id=\"mwRw\">Spree</a> river, which flows into the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Havel\" title=\"Havel\" id=\"mwSA\">Havel</a> in the western borough of <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Spandau\" title=\"Spandau\" id=\"mwSQ\">Spandau</a>. First documented in the 13th century<sup about=\"#mwt70\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-Kleiner-2015_7-1\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{\"name\":\"Kleiner-2015\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-Kleiner-2015-7\" id=\"mwSg\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwSw\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwTA\">[</span>7<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwTQ\">]</span></span></a></sup> and at the crossing of two important historic <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Trade_route\" title=\"Trade route\" id=\"mwTg\">trade routes</a>,<sup about=\"#mwt73\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-Verein_für_die_Geschichte_Berlins-2004_10-0\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{\"name\":\"Verein für die Geschichte Berlins-2004\"},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Verein_für_die_Geschichte_Berlins-2004-10\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-Verein_für_die_Geschichte_Berlins-2004-10\" id=\"mwTw\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwUA\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwUQ\">[</span>9<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwUg\">]</span></span></a></sup> Berlin was designated the capital of the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Margraviate_of_Brandenburg\" title=\"Margraviate of Brandenburg\" id=\"mwUw\">Margraviate of Brandenburg</a> (1417–1701), <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Kingdom_of_Prussia\" title=\"Kingdom of Prussia\" id=\"mwVA\">Kingdom of Prussia</a> (1701–1918), <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./German_Empire\" title=\"German Empire\" id=\"mwVQ\">German Empire</a> (1871–1918), <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Weimar_Republic\" title=\"Weimar Republic\" id=\"mwVg\">Weimar Republic</a> (1919–1933), and <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Nazi_Germany\" title=\"Nazi Germany\" id=\"mwVw\">Nazi Germany</a> (1933–1945). Berlin served as a scientific, artistic, and philosophical hub during the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Age_of_Enlightenment\" title=\"Age of Enlightenment\" id=\"mwWA\">Age of Enlightenment</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Neoclassicism\" title=\"Neoclassicism\" id=\"mwWQ\">Neoclassicism</a>, and the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./German_revolutions_of_1848–1849\" title=\"German revolutions of 1848–1849\" id=\"mwWg\">German revolutions of 1848–1849</a>. During the <i id=\"mwWw\"><a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Gründerzeit\" title=\"Gründerzeit\" id=\"mwXA\">Gründerzeit</a></i>, an industrialization-induced economic boom triggered a rapid population increase in Berlin. <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./1920s_Berlin\" title=\"1920s Berlin\" id=\"mwXQ\">Berlin in the 1920s</a> was the third-largest city in the world by population.<sup about=\"#mwt76\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-11\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-11\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-11\" id=\"mwXg\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwXw\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwYA\">[</span>10<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwYQ\">]</span></span></a></sup></p>\n\n<p id=\"mwYg\">After <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./World_War_II\" title=\"World War II\" id=\"mwYw\">World War II</a> and following Berlin's occupation, the city was split into <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./West_Berlin\" title=\"West Berlin\" id=\"mwZA\">West Berlin</a> and <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./East_Berlin\" title=\"East Berlin\" id=\"mwZQ\">East Berlin</a>, divided by the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berlin_Wall\" title=\"Berlin Wall\" id=\"mwZg\">Berlin Wall</a>.<sup about=\"#mwt79\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-12\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-12\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-12\" id=\"mwZw\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwaA\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwaQ\">[</span>11<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwag\">]</span></span></a></sup> East Berlin was declared the capital of <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./East_Germany\" title=\"East Germany\" id=\"mwaw\">East Germany</a>, while <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Bonn\" title=\"Bonn\" id=\"mwbA\">Bonn</a> became the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./West_Germany\" title=\"West Germany\" id=\"mwbQ\">West German</a> capital. Following <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./German_reunification\" title=\"German reunification\" id=\"mwbg\">German reunification</a> in 1990, Berlin once again became the capital of all of Germany. Due to its geographic location and history, Berlin has been called \"the heart of Europe\".<sup about=\"#mwt82\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-13\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-13\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-13\" id=\"mwbw\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwcA\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwcQ\">[</span>12<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwcg\">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about=\"#mwt85\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-14\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-14\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-14\" id=\"mwcw\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwdA\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwdQ\">[</span>13<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwdg\">]</span></span></a></sup> Berlin is a <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Global_city\" title=\"Global city\" id=\"mwdw\">global city</a> of <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Culture_in_Berlin\" title=\"Culture in Berlin\" id=\"mweA\">culture</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Politics_of_Berlin\" title=\"Politics of Berlin\" id=\"mweQ\">politics</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Media_in_Berlin\" title=\"Media in Berlin\" id=\"mweg\">media</a> and science.<sup about=\"#mwt90\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-15\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-15\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-15\" id=\"mwew\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwfA\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwfQ\">[</span>14<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwfg\">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Economy_of_Berlin\" title=\"Economy of Berlin\" id=\"mwfw\">Its economy</a> is based on <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./High_tech\" title=\"High tech\" id=\"mwgA\">high tech</a> and the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Service_sector\" title=\"Service sector\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwgQ\">service sector</a>, encompassing a diverse range of <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Creative_industries\" title=\"Creative industries\" id=\"mwgg\">creative industries</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Startup_company\" title=\"Startup company\" id=\"mwgw\">startup companies</a>, research facilities, and media corporations. Berlin serves as a continental hub for air and rail traffic and has <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Transport_in_Berlin\" title=\"Transport in Berlin\" id=\"mwhA\">a complex public transportation network</a>. <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Tourism_in_Berlin\" title=\"Tourism in Berlin\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwhQ\">Tourism in Berlin</a> makes the city a popular global destination.<sup about=\"#mwt93\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-16\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-16\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-16\" id=\"mwhg\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwhw\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwiA\">[</span>15<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwiQ\">]</span></span></a></sup></p>\n\n<p id=\"mwig\">Berlin is home to several universities, such as the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Humboldt_University_of_Berlin\" title=\"Humboldt University of Berlin\" id=\"mwiw\">Humboldt University of Berlin</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Technische_Universität_Berlin\" title=\"Technische Universität Berlin\" id=\"mwjA\">Technische Universität Berlin</a>, the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berlin_University_of_the_Arts\" title=\"Berlin University of the Arts\" id=\"mwjQ\">Berlin University of the Arts</a> and the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Free_University_of_Berlin\" title=\"Free University of Berlin\" id=\"mwjg\">Free University of Berlin</a>. The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berlin_Zoological_Garden\" title=\"Berlin Zoological Garden\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwjw\">Berlin Zoological Garden</a> is the most visited zoo in Europe. <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Babelsberg_Studio\" title=\"Babelsberg Studio\" id=\"mwkA\">Babelsberg Studio</a> is the world's first large-scale movie studio complex, and there are <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./List_of_films_set_in_Berlin\" title=\"List of films set in Berlin\" id=\"mwkQ\">many films set in Berlin</a>.<sup about=\"#mwt96\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-17\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-17\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-17\" id=\"mwkg\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwkw\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwlA\">[</span>16<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwlQ\">]</span></span></a></sup> Berlin is home to three <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./UNESCO_World_Heritage_Sites\" title=\"UNESCO World Heritage Sites\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwlg\">UNESCO World Heritage Sites</a>: <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Museum_Island\" title=\"Museum Island\" id=\"mwlw\">Museum Island</a>, the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Palaces_and_Parks_of_Potsdam_and_Berlin\" title=\"Palaces and Parks of Potsdam and Berlin\" id=\"mwmA\">Palaces and Parks of Potsdam and Berlin</a>, and the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berlin_Modernism_Housing_Estates\" title=\"Berlin Modernism Housing Estates\" id=\"mwmQ\">Berlin Modernism Housing Estates</a>.<sup about=\"#mwt99\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-UNESCO_18-0\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{\"name\":\"UNESCO\"},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-UNESCO-18\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-UNESCO-18\" id=\"mwmg\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwmw\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwnA\">[</span>17<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwnQ\">]</span></span></a></sup> Other landmarks include the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Brandenburg_Gate\" title=\"Brandenburg Gate\" id=\"mwng\">Brandenburg Gate</a>, the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Reichstag_building\" title=\"Reichstag building\" id=\"mwnw\">Reichstag building</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Potsdamer_Platz\" title=\"Potsdamer Platz\" id=\"mwoA\">Potsdamer Platz</a>, the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Memorial_to_the_Murdered_Jews_of_Europe\" title=\"Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe\" id=\"mwoQ\">Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe</a>, and the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berlin_Wall_Memorial\" title=\"Berlin Wall Memorial\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwog\">Berlin Wall Memorial</a>. Berlin has <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./List_of_museums_and_galleries_in_Berlin\" title=\"List of museums and galleries in Berlin\" id=\"mwow\">numerous museums, galleries</a>, and libraries. The city includes lakes in the western and southeastern boroughs, the largest of which is <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Müggelsee\" title=\"Müggelsee\" id=\"mwpA\">Müggelsee</a>. About 1/3 of the city's area is composed of forests, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./List_of_parks_and_gardens_in_Berlin\" title=\"List of parks and gardens in Berlin\" id=\"mwpQ\">parks and gardens</a>, rivers, canals, and lakes.<sup about=\"#mwt102\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-Senatsverwaltung_für_Umwelt,_Verkehr_und_Klimaschutz_Berlin,_Referat_Freiraumplanung_und_Stadtgrün_19-0\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw-section-id=\"2\" id=\"mwsA\"><h3 id=\"Etymology\">Etymology</h3>\n<p id=\"mwsQ\">Berlin lies in northeastern Germany, in <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Germania_Slavica\" title=\"Germania Slavica\" id=\"mwsg\">an area formerly settled by Slavs</a> which thus exhibits many (Germanized) Slavic-derived placenames to this day (see below). The word <i id=\"mwsw\">Berlin</i> also has its roots in the language of the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./West_Slavs\" title=\"West Slavs\" id=\"mwtA\">West Slavs</a>, and may be related to the Old <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Polabian_language\" title=\"Polabian language\" id=\"mwtQ\">Polabian</a> stem <span title=\"Polabian-language text\" about=\"#mwt107\" typeof=\"mw:Transclusion\" id=\"mwtg\" data-mw='{\"parts\":[{\"template\":{\"target\":{\"wt\":\"Lang\",\"href\":\"./Template:Lang\"},\"params\":{\"1\":{\"wt\":\"pox\"},\"2\":{\"wt\":\"berl-/birl-\"}},\"i\":0}}]}'><i lang=\"pox\">berl-/birl-</i></span><link rel=\"mw:PageProp/Category\" href=\"./Category:Articles_containing_Polabian-language_text\" about=\"#mwt107\" id=\"mwtw\"/> (\"swamp\").<sup about=\"#mwt110\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-20\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-20\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-20\" id=\"mwuA\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwuQ\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwug\">[</span>19<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwuw\">]</span></span></a></sup></p>\n\n<p id=\"mwvA\">Of Berlin's <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Boroughs_and_neighborhoods_of_Berlin\" title=\"Boroughs and neighborhoods of Berlin\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwvQ\">twelve boroughs</a>, five bear a Slavic-derived name—<a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Pankow\" title=\"Pankow\" id=\"mwvg\">Pankow</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Steglitz-Zehlendorf\" title=\"Steglitz-Zehlendorf\" id=\"mwvw\">Steglitz-Zehlendorf</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Marzahn-Hellersdorf\" title=\"Marzahn-Hellersdorf\" id=\"mwwA\">Marzahn-Hellersdorf</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Treptow-Köpenick\" title=\"Treptow-Köpenick\" id=\"mwwQ\">Treptow-Köpenick</a> and <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Spandau\" title=\"Spandau\" id=\"mwwg\">Spandau</a>; furthermore, across the city's 96 neighborhoods, there are 22 which bear a Slavic-rooted name—<a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Altglienicke\" title=\"Altglienicke\" id=\"mwww\">Altglienicke</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Alt-Treptow\" title=\"Alt-Treptow\" id=\"mwxA\">Alt-Treptow</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Britz\" title=\"Britz\" id=\"mwxQ\">Britz</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Buch_(Berlin)\" title=\"Buch (Berlin)\" id=\"mwxg\">Buch</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Buckow_(Berlin)\" title=\"Buckow (Berlin)\" id=\"mwxw\">Buckow</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Gatow\" title=\"Gatow\" id=\"mwyA\">Gatow</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Karow_(Berlin)\" title=\"Karow (Berlin)\" id=\"mwyQ\">Karow</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Kladow\" title=\"Kladow\" id=\"mwyg\">Kladow</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Köpenick\" title=\"Köpenick\" id=\"mwyw\">Köpenick</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Lankwitz\" title=\"Lankwitz\" id=\"mwzA\">Lankwitz</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Lübars\" title=\"Lübars\" id=\"mwzQ\">Lübars</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Malchow_(Berlin)\" title=\"Malchow (Berlin)\" id=\"mwzg\">Malchow</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Marzahn\" title=\"Marzahn\" id=\"mwzw\">Marzahn</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Pankow_(locality)\" title=\"Pankow (locality)\" id=\"mw0A\">Pankow</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Prenzlauer_Berg\" title=\"Prenzlauer Berg\" id=\"mw0Q\">Prenzlauer Berg</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Rudow\" title=\"Rudow\" id=\"mw0g\">Rudow</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Schmöckwitz\" title=\"Schmöckwitz\" id=\"mw0w\">Schmöckwitz</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Spandau_(locality)\" title=\"Spandau (locality)\" id=\"mw1A\">Spandau</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Stadtrandsiedlung_Malchow\" title=\"Stadtrandsiedlung Malchow\" id=\"mw1Q\">Stadtrandsiedlung Malchow</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Steglitz\" title=\"Steglitz\" id=\"mw1g\">Steglitz</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Tegel\" title=\"Tegel\" id=\"mw1w\">Tegel</a> and <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Zehlendorf_(Berlin)\" title=\"Zehlendorf (Berlin)\" id=\"mw2A\">Zehlendorf</a>.</p>\n\n</section><section data-mw-section-id=\"3\" id=\"mw2Q\"><h3 id=\"Prehistory\">Prehistory</h3>\n<p id=\"mw2g\">The area of what is now Berlin has been settled for millennia.<sup about=\"#mwt113\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-21\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-21\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-21\" id=\"mw2w\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mw3A\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mw3Q\">[</span>20<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mw3g\">]</span></span></a></sup> A deer mask, dated to 9,000 BCE, is attributed to the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Maglemosian_culture\" title=\"Maglemosian culture\" id=\"mw3w\">Maglemosian culture</a>. Around 2,000 BCE dense human settlements along the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Spree_(river)\" title=\"Spree (river)\" id=\"mw4A\">Spree</a> and <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Havel\" title=\"Havel\" id=\"mw4Q\">Havel</a> rivers gave rise to the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Lusatian_culture\" title=\"Lusatian culture\" id=\"mw4g\">Lusatian culture</a>.<sup about=\"#mwt116\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-22\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-22\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-22\" id=\"mw4w\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mw5A\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mw5Q\">[</span>21<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mw5g\">]</span></span></a></sup> Starting around 500 BCE <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Germanic_tribes\" title=\"Germanic tribes\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mw5w\">Germanic tribes</a> settled in a number of villages in the higher situated areas of today's Berlin. After the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Semnones\" title=\"Semnones\" id=\"mw6A\">Semnones</a> left around 200 CE, the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Burgundians\" title=\"Burgundians\" id=\"mw6Q\">Burgundians</a> followed. In the 7th century <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Slavic_tribes\" title=\"Slavic tribes\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mw6g\">Slavic tribes</a>, the later known <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Hevelli\" title=\"Hevelli\" id=\"mw6w\">Hevelli</a> and <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Sprevane\" title=\"Sprevane\" id=\"mw7A\">Sprevane</a>, reached the region.</p>\n\n</section><section data-mw-section-id=\"4\" id=\"mw7Q\"><h3 id=\"12th_century_to_16th_century\">12th century to 16th century</h3>\n<figure class=\"mw-default-size mw-halign-left\" typeof=\"mw:File/Thumb\" id=\"mw7g\"><a href=\"./File:Seal_Berlin_1253.png\" class=\"mw-file-description\" id=\"mw7w\"><img resource=\"./File:Seal_Berlin_1253.png\" src=\"//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/19/Seal_Berlin_1253.png/250px-Seal_Berlin_1253.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail\" decoding=\"async\" loading=\"lazy\" srcset=\"//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/19/Seal_Berlin_1253.png/500px-Seal_Berlin_1253.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x\" data-file-width=\"832\" data-file-height=\"893\" data-file-type=\"bitmap\" height=\"204\" width=\"190\" class=\"mw-file-element mw-file-upright\" style=\"--mw-file-upright: 0.75\" id=\"mw8A\"/></a><figcaption id=\"mw8Q\">The oldest seal of Berlin, dating back to 1253</figcaption></figure>\n\n<p id=\"mw8g\">In the 12th century the region came under German rule as part of the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Margraviate_of_Brandenburg\" title=\"Margraviate of Brandenburg\" id=\"mw8w\">Margraviate of Brandenburg</a>, founded by <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Albert_the_Bear\" title=\"Albert the Bear\" id=\"mw9A\">Albert the Bear</a> in 1157. The first written records of towns in the area of present-day Berlin date from the late 12th century. <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Spandau\" title=\"Spandau\" id=\"mw9Q\">Spandau</a> is first mentioned in 1197 and <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Köpenick\" title=\"Köpenick\" id=\"mw9g\">Köpenick</a> in 1209.<sup about=\"#mwt119\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-23\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-23\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-23\" id=\"mw9w\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mw-A\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mw-Q\">[</span>22<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mw-g\">]</span></span></a></sup> German merchants founded two settlements in today's city center – Berlin (or <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Alt-Berlin\" title=\"Alt-Berlin\" id=\"mw-w\">Alt-Berlin</a>; at the site of today's <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Nikolaiviertel\" title=\"Nikolaiviertel\" id=\"mw_A\">Nikolaiviertel</a>) and <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Cölln\" title=\"Cölln\" id=\"mw_Q\">Cölln</a> (on the island in the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Spree_(river)\" title=\"Spree (river)\" id=\"mw_g\">Spree</a> now known as <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Museum_Island\" title=\"Museum Island\" id=\"mw_w\">Museum Island</a>). 1237 is considered the founding date of the city.<sup about=\"#mwt122\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-24\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-24\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-24\" id=\"mwAQA\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAQE\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAQI\">[</span>23<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAQM\">]</span></span></a></sup> Berlin and Cölln over time formed close economic and social ties, and profited from the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Stapelrecht\" title=\"Stapelrecht\" id=\"mwAQQ\">staple right</a> on the two important <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Trade_route\" title=\"Trade route\" id=\"mwAQU\">trade routes</a>. One was known as <i id=\"mwAQY\"><a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Via_Imperii\" title=\"Via Imperii\" id=\"mwAQc\">Via Imperii</a></i>, and the other trade route reached from <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Bruges\" title=\"Bruges\" id=\"mwAQg\">Bruges</a> to <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Novgorod\" title=\"Novgorod\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwAQk\">Novgorod</a>.<sup about=\"#mwt123\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-Verein_für_die_Geschichte_Berlins-2004_10-1\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{\"name\":\"Verein für die Geschichte Berlins-2004\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-Verein_für_die_Geschichte_Berlins-2004-10\" id=\"mwAQo\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAQs\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAQw\">[</span>9<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAQ0\">]</span></span></a></sup> In 1307, the two towns formed an alliance with a common external policy, their internal administrations still being separated.<sup about=\"#mwt126\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-Stöver_B_25-0\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{\"name\":\"Stöver B\"},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Stöver_B-25\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-Stöver_B-25\" id=\"mwAQ4\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAQ8\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwARA\">[</span>24<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwARE\">]</span></span></a></sup> In 1326, the territory of Berlin was raided by <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Baltic_paganism\" title=\"Baltic paganism\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwARI\">pagan</a> <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Lithuanians\" title=\"Lithuanians\" id=\"mwARM\">Lithuanians</a> during the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Raid_on_Brandenburg\" title=\"Raid on Brandenburg\" id=\"mwARQ\">Raid on Brandenburg</a>.</p>\n\n<p id=\"mwARU\">Members of the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Hohenzollern\" title=\"Hohenzollern\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwARY\">Hohenzollern</a> family ruled in Berlin until 1918, first as electors of Brandenburg, then as kings of <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Prussia\" title=\"Prussia\" id=\"mwARc\">Prussia</a>, and eventually as <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./German_emperor\" title=\"German emperor\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwARg\">German emperors</a>. In 1443, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Frederick_II_of_Brandenburg\" title=\"Frederick II of Brandenburg\" id=\"mwARk\">Frederick II of Brandenburg</a> initiated the construction of a <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Stadtschloss,_Berlin\" title=\"Stadtschloss, Berlin\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwARo\">new royal palace</a> in the twin city of Berlin-Cölln. The protests of the town citizens against the building culminated in 1448, in the \"Berlin Indignation\" (<span about=\"#mwt127\" typeof=\"mw:Transclusion\" id=\"mwARs\" data-mw='{\"parts\":[{\"template\":{\"target\":{\"wt\":\"langx\",\"href\":\"./Template:Langx\"},\"params\":{\"1\":{\"wt\":\"de\"},\"2\":{\"wt\":\"Berliner Unwille\"},\"links\":{\"wt\":\"no\"}},\"i\":0}}]}'>German: </span><i lang=\"de\" about=\"#mwt127\">Berliner Unwille</i><link rel=\"mw:PageProp/Category\" href=\"./Category:Articles_containing_German-language_text\" about=\"#mwt127\" id=\"mwARw\"/>).<sup about=\"#mwt130\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-26\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-26\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-26\" id=\"mwAR0\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAR4\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAR8\">[</span>25<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwASA\">]</span></span></a></sup> Officially, the Berlin-Cölln palace became the permanent residence of the Brandenburg electors of the Hohenzollern dynasty in 1486, when <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./John_Cicero\" title=\"John Cicero\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwASE\">John Cicero</a> took power.<sup about=\"#mwt133\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-27\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-27\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-27\" id=\"mwASI\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwASM\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwASQ\">[</span>26<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwASU\">]</span></span></a></sup> Berlin-Cölln, however, had to give up its status as a free <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Hanseatic_League\" title=\"Hanseatic League\" id=\"mwASY\">Hanseatic League</a> city. In 1539, the electors and the city officially became <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Lutheran\" title=\"Lutheran\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwASc\">Lutheran</a>.<sup about=\"#mwt136\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-28\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-28\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-28\" id=\"mwASg\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwASk\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwASo\">[</span>27<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwASs\">]</span></span></a></sup></p>\n\n</section><section data-mw-section-id=\"5\" id=\"mwASw\"><h3 id=\"17th_to_19th_centuries\">17th to 19th centuries</h3>\n<figure class=\"mw-default-size\" typeof=\"mw:File/Thumb\" id=\"mwAS0\"><a href=\"./File:Reichstagsgebaeude.jpg\" class=\"mw-file-description\" id=\"mwAS4\"><img resource=\"./File:Reichstagsgebaeude.jpg\" src=\"//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/Reichstagsgebaeude.jpg/250px-Reichstagsgebaeude.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail\" decoding=\"async\" loading=\"lazy\" srcset=\"//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/Reichstagsgebaeude.jpg/500px-Reichstagsgebaeude.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x\" data-file-width=\"3480\" data-file-height=\"2572\" data-file-type=\"bitmap\" height=\"185\" width=\"250\" class=\"mw-file-element\" id=\"mwAS8\"/></a><figcaption id=\"mwATA\"><a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Reichstag_building\" title=\"Reichstag building\" id=\"mwATE\">Reichstag building</a> at the end of the 19th century</figcaption></figure>\n\n<p id=\"mwATI\">The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Thirty_Years'_War\" title=\"Thirty Years' War\" id=\"mwATM\">Thirty Years' War</a> between 1618 and 1648 devastated Berlin. One third of its houses were damaged or destroyed, and the city lost half of its population.<sup about=\"#mwt139\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-29\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-29\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-29\" id=\"mwATQ\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwATU\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwATY\">[</span>28<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwATc\">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Frederick_William_I,_Elector_of_Brandenburg\" title=\"Frederick William I, Elector of Brandenburg\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwATg\">Frederick William</a>, known as the \"Great Elector\", who had succeeded his father <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./George_William,_Elector_of_Brandenburg\" title=\"George William, Elector of Brandenburg\" id=\"mwATk\">George William</a> as ruler in 1640, initiated a policy of promoting immigration and religious tolerance.<sup about=\"#mwt142\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-30\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-30\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-30\" id=\"mwATo\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwATs\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwATw\">[</span>29<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAT0\">]</span></span></a></sup> With the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Edict_of_Potsdam\" title=\"Edict of Potsdam\" id=\"mwAT4\">Edict of Potsdam</a> in 1685, Frederick William offered asylum to the French <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Huguenot\" title=\"Huguenot\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwAT8\">Huguenots</a>.<sup about=\"#mwt145\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-31\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-31\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-31\" id=\"mwAUA\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAUE\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAUI\">[</span>30<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAUM\">]</span></span></a></sup></p>\n\n<p id=\"mwAUQ\">By 1700, approximately 30 percent of Berlin's residents were French, because of the Huguenot immigration.<sup about=\"#mwt148\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-32\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-32\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-32\" id=\"mwAUU\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAUY\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAUc\">[</span>31<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAUg\">]</span></span></a></sup> Many other immigrants came from <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Bohemia\" title=\"Bohemia\" id=\"mwAUk\">Bohemia</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Polish–Lithuanian_Commonwealth\" title=\"Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth\" id=\"mwAUo\">Poland</a>, and <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Prince-Archbishopric_of_Salzburg\" title=\"Prince-Archbishopric of Salzburg\" id=\"mwAUs\">Salzburg</a>.<sup about=\"#mwt151\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-33\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-33\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-33\" id=\"mwAUw\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAU0\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAU4\">[</span>32<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAU8\">]</span></span></a></sup></p>\n\n<p id=\"mwAVA\">Since 1618, the Margraviate of Brandenburg had been in <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Personal_union\" title=\"Personal union\" id=\"mwAVE\">personal union</a> with the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Duchy_of_Prussia\" title=\"Duchy of Prussia\" id=\"mwAVI\">Duchy of Prussia</a>. In 1701, the dual state formed the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Kingdom_of_Prussia\" title=\"Kingdom of Prussia\" id=\"mwAVM\">Kingdom of Prussia</a>, as <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Frederick_III,_Elector_of_Brandenburg\" title=\"Frederick III, Elector of Brandenburg\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwAVQ\">Frederick III, Elector of Brandenburg</a>, crowned himself as king <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Frederick_I_of_Prussia\" title=\"Frederick I of Prussia\" id=\"mwAVU\">Frederick I in Prussia</a>. Berlin became the capital of the new Kingdom,<sup about=\"#mwt152\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-34\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-34\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-34\" id=\"mwAVY\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAVc\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAVg\">[</span>33<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAVk\">]</span></span></a></sup> replacing <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Königsberg\" title=\"Königsberg\" id=\"mwAVo\">Königsberg</a>. This was a successful attempt to centralise the capital in the very far-flung state, and it was the first time the city began to grow. In 1709, Berlin merged with the four cities of Cölln, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Friedrichswerder\" title=\"Friedrichswerder\" id=\"mwAVs\">Friedrichswerder</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Friedrichstadt_(Berlin)\" title=\"Friedrichstadt (Berlin)\" id=\"mwAVw\">Friedrichstadt</a> and <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Dorotheenstadt\" title=\"Dorotheenstadt\" id=\"mwAV0\">Dorotheenstadt</a> under the name Berlin, \"Haupt- und Residenzstadt Berlin\".<sup about=\"#mwt153\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-Stöver_B_25-1\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{\"name\":\"Stöver B\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-Stöver_B-25\" id=\"mwAV4\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAV8\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAWA\">[</span>24<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAWE\">]</span></span></a></sup> Between 1700 and 1750, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Demographics_of_Berlin\" title=\"Demographics of Berlin\" id=\"mwAWI\">Berlin's population nearly quadrupled</a>, rising from about 30,000 to 113,000.</p>\n\n<p id=\"mwAWM\">In 1740, Frederick II, known as <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Frederick_the_Great\" title=\"Frederick the Great\" id=\"mwAWQ\">Frederick the Great</a> (1740–1786), came to power.<sup about=\"#mwt156\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-35\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-35\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-35\" id=\"mwAWU\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAWY\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAWc\">[</span>34<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAWg\">]</span></span></a></sup> Under the rule of Frederick II, Berlin became a center of <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./The_Enlightenment\" title=\"The Enlightenment\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwAWk\">the Enlightenment</a>, but also, was briefly occupied during the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Seven_Years'_War\" title=\"Seven Years' War\" id=\"mwAWo\">Seven Years' War</a> by the Russian army.<sup about=\"#mwt159\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-36\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-36\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-36\" id=\"mwAWs\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAWw\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAW0\">[</span>35<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAW4\">]</span></span></a></sup> Following France's victory in the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./War_of_the_Fourth_Coalition\" title=\"War of the Fourth Coalition\" id=\"mwAW8\">War of the Fourth Coalition</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Napoleon_Bonaparte\" title=\"Napoleon Bonaparte\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwAXA\">Napoleon Bonaparte</a> <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Fall_of_Berlin_(1806)\" title=\"Fall of Berlin (1806)\" id=\"mwAXE\">marched into Berlin in 1806</a>, but granted self-government to the city.<sup about=\"#mwt162\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-37\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-37\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-37\" id=\"mwAXI\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAXM\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAXQ\">[</span>36<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAXU\">]</span></span></a></sup> In 1815, the city became part of the new <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Province_of_Brandenburg\" title=\"Province of Brandenburg\" id=\"mwAXY\">Province of Brandenburg</a>.<sup about=\"#mwt165\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-38\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-38\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-38\" id=\"mwAXc\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAXg\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAXk\">[</span>37<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAXo\">]</span></span></a></sup></p>\n\n<p id=\"mwAXs\">The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Industrial_Revolution\" title=\"Industrial Revolution\" id=\"mwAXw\">Industrial Revolution</a> transformed Berlin during the 19th century; the city's economy and population expanded dramatically, and it became the main railway hub and economic center of Germany. Additional suburbs soon developed and increased the area and population of Berlin. In 1861, neighboring suburbs including <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Wedding_(Berlin)\" title=\"Wedding (Berlin)\" id=\"mwAX0\">Wedding</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Moabit\" title=\"Moabit\" id=\"mwAX4\">Moabit</a> and several others were incorporated into Berlin.<sup about=\"#mwt168\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-39\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-39\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-39\" id=\"mwAX8\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAYA\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAYE\">[</span>38<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAYI\">]</span></span></a></sup> In 1871, Berlin became capital of the newly founded <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./German_Empire\" title=\"German Empire\" id=\"mwAYM\">German Empire</a>.<sup about=\"#mwt171\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-40\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-40\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-40\" id=\"mwAYQ\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAYU\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAYY\">[</span>39<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAYc\">]</span></span></a></sup> In 1881, it became a city district separate from <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Brandenburg\" title=\"Brandenburg\" id=\"mwAYg\">Brandenburg</a>.<sup about=\"#mwt174\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-41\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-41\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-41\" id=\"mwAYk\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAYo\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAYs\">[</span>40<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAYw\">]</span></span></a></sup></p>\n\n</section><section data-mw-section-id=\"6\" id=\"mwAY0\"><h3 id=\"1900–1945\"><span id=\"1900.E2.80.931945\" typeof=\"mw:FallbackId\"></span>1900–1945</h3>\n<span class=\"mw-empty-elt\" about=\"#mwt175\" typeof=\"mw:Transclusion\" id=\"mwAY4\" data-mw='{\"parts\":[{\"template\":{\"target\":{\"wt\":\"Further\",\"href\":\"./Template:Further\"},\"params\":{\"1\":{\"wt\":\"Greater Berlin Act\"},\"2\":{\"wt\":\"1920s Berlin\"},\"3\":{\"wt\":\"Battle of Berlin\"},\"4\":{\"wt\":\"West Berlin\"},\"5\":{\"wt\":\"East Berlin\"}},\"i\":0}}]}'><link rel=\"mw-deduplicated-inline-style\" href=\"mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1368532237\" about=\"#mwt176\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/templatestyles\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"templatestyles\",\"attrs\":{\"src\":\"Module:Hatnote/styles.css\"},\"body\":{\"extsrc\":\"\"}}'/></span><div role=\"note\" class=\"hatnote navigation-not-searchable\" about=\"#mwt175\" id=\"mwAY8\">Further information: <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Greater_Berlin_Act\" title=\"Greater Berlin Act\">Greater Berlin Act</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./1920s_Berlin\" title=\"1920s Berlin\">1920s Berlin</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Battle_of_Berlin\" title=\"Battle of Berlin\">Battle of Berlin</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./West_Berlin\" title=\"West Berlin\">West Berlin</a>, and <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./East_Berlin\" title=\"East Berlin\">East Berlin</a></div>\n\n<figure class=\"mw-default-size mw-halign-left\" typeof=\"mw:File/Thumb\" id=\"mwAZA\"><a href=\"./File:Revolutie_in_Duitsland,_SFA022823451.jpg\" class=\"mw-file-description\" id=\"mwAZE\"><img resource=\"./File:Revolutie_in_Duitsland,_SFA022823451.jpg\" src=\"//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cf/Revolutie_in_Duitsland%2C_SFA022823451.jpg/250px-Revolutie_in_Duitsland%2C_SFA022823451.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail\" decoding=\"async\" loading=\"lazy\" srcset=\"//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cf/Revolutie_in_Duitsland%2C_SFA022823451.jpg/500px-Revolutie_in_Duitsland%2C_SFA022823451.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x\" data-file-width=\"3612\" data-file-height=\"2520\" data-file-type=\"bitmap\" height=\"174\" width=\"250\" class=\"mw-file-element\" id=\"mwAZI\"/></a><figcaption id=\"mwAZM\"><a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./German_Revolution\" title=\"German Revolution\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwAZQ\">German Revolution</a> in Berlin in 1918</figcaption></figure>\n\n<p id=\"mwAZU\">In the early 20th century, Berlin had become a fertile ground for the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./German_Expressionism\" title=\"German Expressionism\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwAZY\">German Expressionist</a> movement.<sup about=\"#mwt179\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-42\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-42\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-42\" id=\"mwAZc\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAZg\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAZk\">[</span>41<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAZo\">]</span></span></a></sup> In fields such as architecture, painting and cinema new forms of artistic styles were invented.</p>\n\n<p id=\"mwAZs\">At the end of <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./World_War_I\" title=\"World War I\" id=\"mwAZw\">World War I</a>, during the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./German_Revolution\" title=\"German Revolution\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwAZ0\">German Revolution</a>, the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Weimar_Republic\" title=\"Weimar Republic\" id=\"mwAZ4\">Weimar Republic</a> was proclaimed by <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Philipp_Scheidemann\" title=\"Philipp Scheidemann\" id=\"mwAZ8\">Philipp Scheidemann</a> at the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Reichstag_(building)\" title=\"Reichstag (building)\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwAaA\">Reichstag building</a> on November 9, 1918. In 1920, the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Greater_Berlin_Act\" title=\"Greater Berlin Act\" id=\"mwAaE\">Greater Berlin Act</a> incorporated dozens of suburban cities, villages, and estates around Berlin into an expanded city. The act increased the area of Berlin from <span about=\"#mwt180\" typeof=\"mw:Transclusion\" id=\"mwAaI\" data-mw='{\"parts\":[{\"template\":{\"target\":{\"wt\":\"cvt\",\"href\":\"./Template:Cvt\"},\"params\":{\"1\":{\"wt\":\"66\"},\"2\":{\"wt\":\"to\"},\"3\":{\"wt\":\"883\"},\"4\":{\"wt\":\"km2\"}},\"i\":0}}]}'>66 to 883</span><span typeof=\"mw:Entity\" about=\"#mwt180\"> </span><span about=\"#mwt180\">km</span><sup about=\"#mwt180\">2</sup><span about=\"#mwt180\"> (25 to 341</span><span typeof=\"mw:Entity\" about=\"#mwt180\"> </span><span about=\"#mwt180\">sq</span><span typeof=\"mw:Entity\" about=\"#mwt180\"> </span><span about=\"#mwt180\">mi)</span>. The population almost doubled, and Berlin had a population of around four million. During the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Weimar_culture\" title=\"Weimar culture\" id=\"mwAaM\">Weimar era</a>, Berlin underwent political unrest due to economic uncertainties but also became a renowned center of the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Roaring_Twenties\" title=\"Roaring Twenties\" id=\"mwAaQ\">Roaring Twenties</a>. The metropolis experienced its heyday as a major world capital and was known for its leadership roles in science, technology, arts, the humanities, city planning, film, higher education, government, and industries. <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Albert_Einstein\" title=\"Albert Einstein\" id=\"mwAaU\">Albert Einstein</a> rose to public prominence during his years in Berlin,<sup about=\"#mwt183\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-43\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-43\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-43\" id=\"mwAaY\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAac\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAag\">[</span>42<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAak\">]</span></span></a></sup> being awarded the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Nobel_Prize_for_Physics\" title=\"Nobel Prize for Physics\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwAao\">Nobel Prize for Physics</a> in 1921.<sup about=\"#mwt186\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-44\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-44\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-44\" id=\"mwAas\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAaw\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAa0\">[</span>43<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAa4\">]</span></span></a></sup></p>\n\n<p id=\"mwAa8\">In 1933, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Adolf_Hitler\" title=\"Adolf Hitler\" id=\"mwAbA\">Adolf Hitler</a> and the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Nazi_Party\" title=\"Nazi Party\" id=\"mwAbE\">Nazi Party</a> <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Nazis_came_to_power\" title=\"Nazis came to power\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwAbI\">came to power</a>. Hitler wished for a <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./German_Reich\" title=\"German Reich\" id=\"mwAbM\">German Reich</a> with a capital city that had a monumental ensemble.<sup about=\"#mwt189\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-donath_45-0\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{\"name\":\"donath\"},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-donath-45\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-donath-45\" id=\"mwAbQ\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAbU\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAbY\">[</span>44<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAbc\">]</span></span></a></sup> The National Socialist regime embarked on monumental construction projects in Berlin as a way to express their power and authority through <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Nazi_architecture\" title=\"Nazi architecture\" id=\"mwAbg\">architecture</a>.<sup about=\"#mwt190\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-donath_45-1\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{\"name\":\"donath\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-donath-45\" id=\"mwAbk\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAbo\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAbs\">[</span>44<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAbw\">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Adolf_Hitler\" title=\"Adolf Hitler\" id=\"mwAb0\">Adolf Hitler</a> and <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Albert_Speer\" title=\"Albert Speer\" id=\"mwAb4\">Albert Speer</a> developed architectural concepts for the conversion of the city into <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Germania_(city)\" title=\"Germania (city)\" id=\"mwAb8\">World Capital Germania</a>; these were never implemented.<sup about=\"#mwt191\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-donath_45-2\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{\"name\":\"donath\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-donath-45\" id=\"mwAcA\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAcE\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAcI\">[</span>44<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAcM\">]</span></span></a></sup> Berlin hosted the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./1936_Summer_Olympics\" title=\"1936 Summer Olympics\" id=\"mwAcQ\">1936 Summer Olympics</a> for which the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Olympiastadion_(Berlin)\" title=\"Olympiastadion (Berlin)\" id=\"mwAcU\">Olympic stadium</a> was built.<sup about=\"#mwt193\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-46\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-46\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-46\" id=\"mwAcY\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAcc\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAcg\">[</span>45<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAck\">]</span></span></a></sup></p>\n\n<p id=\"mwAco\">NSDAP rule diminished Berlin's Jewish community from 160,000 (one-third of all Jews in the country) to about 80,000 due to emigration between 1933 and 1939. After <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Kristallnacht\" title=\"Kristallnacht\" id=\"mwAcs\">Kristallnacht</a> in 1938, thousands of the city's Jews were imprisoned in the nearby <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Sachsenhausen_concentration_camp\" title=\"Sachsenhausen concentration camp\" id=\"mwAcw\">Sachsenhausen concentration camp</a>. Starting in early 1943, many were deported to <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Jewish_ghettos_established_by_Nazi_Germany\" title=\"Jewish ghettos established by Nazi Germany\" id=\"mwAc0\">ghettos</a> like <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Łódź_Ghetto\" title=\"Łódź Ghetto\" id=\"mwAc4\">Łódź</a>, and to <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Concentration_camp\" title=\"Concentration camp\" id=\"mwAc8\">concentration</a> and <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Extermination_camp\" title=\"Extermination camp\" id=\"mwAdA\">extermination camps</a> such as <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Auschwitz\" title=\"Auschwitz\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwAdE\">Auschwitz</a>.<sup about=\"#mwt196\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-47\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-47\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-47\" id=\"mwAdI\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAdM\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAdQ\">[</span>46<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAdU\">]</span></span></a></sup> During <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./World_War_II\" title=\"World War II\" id=\"mwAdY\">World War II</a>, Berlin was the location of multiple Nazi prisons, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Forced_labour_under_German_rule_during_World_War_II\" title=\"Forced labour under German rule during World War II\" id=\"mwAdc\">forced labor</a> camps, 17 subcamps of the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Sachsenhausen_concentration_camp\" title=\"Sachsenhausen concentration camp\" id=\"mwAdg\">Sachsenhausen concentration camp</a> for men and women, including teenagers, of various nationalities,<sup about=\"#mwt199\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-48\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-48\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-48\" id=\"mwAdk\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAdo\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAds\">[</span>47<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAdw\">]</span></span></a></sup> a camp for <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Sinti\" title=\"Sinti\" id=\"mwAd0\">Sinti</a> and Romani people (see <i id=\"mwAd4\"><a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Romani_Holocaust\" title=\"Romani Holocaust\" id=\"mwAd8\">Romani Holocaust</a></i>),<sup about=\"#mwt202\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-49\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-49\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-49\" id=\"mwAeA\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAeE\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAeI\">[</span>48<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAeM\">]</span></span></a></sup> and the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Stalag_III-D\" title=\"Stalag III-D\" id=\"mwAeQ\">Stalag III-D</a> <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./German_prisoner-of-war_camps_in_World_War_II\" title=\"German prisoner-of-war camps in World War II\" id=\"mwAeU\">prisoner-of-war camp</a> for Allied POWs of various nationalities.</p>\n\n<p id=\"mwAeY\">Parts of Berlin – including large parts of the city center – were destroyed in the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Bombing_of_Berlin\" title=\"Bombing of Berlin\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwAec\">bombing of Berlin</a> by Allied air raids in <span about=\"#mwt203\" typeof=\"mw:Transclusion\" id=\"mwAeg\" data-mw='{\"parts\":[{\"template\":{\"target\":{\"wt\":\"Dash year\",\"href\":\"./Template:Dash_year\"},\"params\":{\"1\":{\"wt\":\"1943\"},\"2\":{\"wt\":\"1945\"}},\"i\":0}}]}'>1943–45</span> and the 1945 <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Battle_of_Berlin\" title=\"Battle of Berlin\" id=\"mwAek\">Battle of Berlin</a>. The Allies dropped 67,607 tons of bombs on the city, destroying 6,427 acres (26 km<sup id=\"mwAeo\">2</sup>) of the built-up area. Around 125,000 civilians were killed.<sup about=\"#mwt206\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-50\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-50\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-50\" id=\"mwAes\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAew\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAe0\">[</span>49<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAe4\">]</span></span></a></sup> After the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./End_of_World_War_II_in_Europe\" title=\"End of World War II in Europe\" id=\"mwAe8\">end of World War II in Europe</a> in May 1945, Berlin received large numbers of refugees from the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Former_eastern_territories_of_Germany\" title=\"Former eastern territories of Germany\" id=\"mwAfA\">former eastern territories of Germany</a>. The victorious powers divided the city into four sectors, in a similar way to <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Allied-occupied_Germany\" title=\"Allied-occupied Germany\" id=\"mwAfE\">Allied-occupied Germany</a>. The sectors of the western allies (the United States, the United Kingdom, and France) formed <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./West_Berlin\" title=\"West Berlin\" id=\"mwAfI\">West Berlin</a>, while the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Soviet_Union\" title=\"Soviet Union\" id=\"mwAfM\">Soviet sector</a> formed <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./East_Berlin\" title=\"East Berlin\" id=\"mwAfQ\">East Berlin</a>.<sup about=\"#mwt209\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-51\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-51\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-51\" id=\"mwAfU\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAfY\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAfc\">[</span>50<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAfg\">]</span></span></a></sup></p>\n\n</section><section data-mw-section-id=\"7\" id=\"mwAfk\"><h3 id=\"1946–Present\"><span id=\"1946.E2.80.93Present\" typeof=\"mw:FallbackId\"></span>1946–Present</h3>\n<span class=\"mw-empty-elt\" about=\"#mwt210\" typeof=\"mw:Transclusion\" id=\"mwAfo\" data-mw='{\"parts\":[{\"template\":{\"target\":{\"wt\":\"multiple image\\n\",\"href\":\"./Template:Multiple_image\"},\"params\":{\"align\":{\"wt\":\"right\"},\"image1\":{\"wt\":\"US Army tanks face 2x\" data-file-width=\"1200\" data-file-height=\"913\" data-file-type=\"bitmap\" height=\"158\" width=\"208\" class=\"mw-file-element\"/></a></span></div><div class=\"thumbcaption\">The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berlin_Wall\" title=\"Berlin Wall\">Berlin Wall</a> (painted on the western side) was a barrier that divided the city from 1961 to 1989.</div></div></div></div></div>\n\n<p id=\"mwAfw\">All four Allies of World War II shared administrative responsibilities for Berlin. However, in 1948, when the Western Allies extended the currency reform in the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Trizone\" title=\"Trizone\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwAf0\">Trizone</a> to the three western sectors of Berlin, the Soviet Union imposed the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berlin_Blockade\" title=\"Berlin Blockade\" id=\"mwAf4\">Berlin Blockade</a> on the access routes to and from West Berlin, which lay entirely inside Soviet-controlled territory. The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berlin_airlift\" title=\"Berlin airlift\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwAf8\">Berlin airlift</a>, conducted by the three western Allies, overcame this blockade by supplying food and other supplies to the city from June 1948 to May 1949.<sup about=\"#mwt214\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-52\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-52\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-52\" id=\"mwAgA\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAgE\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAgI\">[</span>51<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAgM\">]</span></span></a></sup></p>\n\n<p id=\"mwAgQ\">The founding of <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./East_Germany\" title=\"East Germany\" id=\"mwAgU\">East</a> and <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./West_Germany\" title=\"West Germany\" id=\"mwAgY\">West Germany</a> in 1949 increased <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Cold_War\" title=\"Cold War\" id=\"mwAgc\">Cold War</a> tensions. West Berlin was surrounded by East German territory, and East Germany proclaimed the eastern part as its capital, a move the western powers did not recognize. East Berlin included most of the city's historic center. The West German government established itself in <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Bonn\" title=\"Bonn\" id=\"mwAgg\">Bonn</a>.<sup about=\"#mwt217\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-53\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-53\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-53\" id=\"mwAgk\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAgo\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAgs\">[</span>52<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAgw\">]</span></span></a></sup> In 1961, East Germany began to build the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berlin_Wall\" title=\"Berlin Wall\" id=\"mwAg0\">Berlin Wall</a> around West Berlin, and events escalated to a tank standoff at <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Checkpoint_Charlie\" title=\"Checkpoint Charlie\" id=\"mwAg4\">Checkpoint Charlie</a>. West Berlin was now de facto a part of West Germany with a unique legal status, while East Berlin was de facto a part of East Germany. <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./John_F._Kennedy\" title=\"John F. Kennedy\" id=\"mwAg8\">John F. Kennedy</a> gave his \"<i id=\"mwAhA\"><a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Ich_bin_ein_Berliner\" title=\"Ich bin ein Berliner\" id=\"mwAhE\">Ich bin ein Berliner</a></i>\" speech on 26 June 1963, underlining the US support for West Berlin.<sup about=\"#mwt220\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-54\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-54\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-54\" id=\"mwAhI\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAhM\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAhQ\">[</span>53<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAhU\">]</span></span></a></sup> Although it was possible for Westerners to pass to the other side through strictly controlled checkpoints, for most Easterners travel to West Berlin or West Germany was prohibited by the East German government. In 1971, a <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Four_Power_Agreement_on_Berlin\" title=\"Four Power Agreement on Berlin\" id=\"mwAhY\">Four-Power Agreement</a> guaranteed access to and from West Berlin by car or train through East Germany.<sup about=\"#mwt223\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-55\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-55\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-55\" id=\"mwAhc\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAhg\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAhk\">[</span>54<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAho\">]</span></span></a></sup></p>\n\n<p id=\"mwAhs\">In 1989, with the end of the Cold War and pressure from the East German population, the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Fall_of_the_Berlin_Wall\" title=\"Fall of the Berlin Wall\" id=\"mwAhw\">Berlin Wall fell</a> on 9 November and was subsequently mostly demolished. On 3 October 1990, the two parts of Germany were <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./German_reunification\" title=\"German reunification\" id=\"mwAh0\">reunified</a> as the Federal Republic of Germany, and Berlin again became a united city. After the fall of the Berlin Wall, the city experienced significant urban development.<sup about=\"#mwt224\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-56\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-56\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-56\" id=\"mwAh4\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAh8\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAiA\">[</span>55<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAiE\">]</span></span></a></sup></p>\n\n<p id=\"mwAiI\"><a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Walter_Momper\" title=\"Walter Momper\" id=\"mwAiM\">Walter Momper</a>, the mayor of West Berlin, became the first mayor of the reunified city in the interim.<sup about=\"#mwt227\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-57\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-57\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-57\" id=\"mwAiQ\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAiU\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAiY\">[</span>56<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAic\">]</span></span></a></sup> City-wide elections in December 1990 resulted in the first \"all Berlin\" mayor being elected to take office in January 1991, with the separate offices of mayors in East and West Berlin expiring by that time, and <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Eberhard_Diepgen\" title=\"Eberhard Diepgen\" id=\"mwAig\">Eberhard Diepgen</a> (a former mayor of West Berlin) became the first elected mayor of a reunited Berlin.<sup about=\"#mwt230\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-58\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-58\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-58\" id=\"mwAik\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAio\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAis\">[</span>57<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAiw\">]</span></span></a></sup></p>\n\n<span class=\"mw-empty-elt\" id=\"mwAjA\">reunified Berlin</a>.<sup about=\"#mwt235\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-59\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-59\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-59\" id=\"mwAjE\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAjI\"><span id=\"mwAjU\">Bundestag</a> (lower house of the German Parliament) <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Decision_on_the_Capital_of_Germany\" title=\"Decision on the Capital of Germany\" id=\"mwAjY\">voted to move the seat</a> of the German capital from Bonn to Berlin, and this was completed in 1999.<sup about=\"#mwt238\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-60\" rel=\"dc:references\" id=\"mwAmg\"><h3 id=\"Topography\">Topography</h3>\n<figure class=\"mw-default-size\" typeof=\"mw:File/Thumb\" id=\"mwAmk\"><a href=\"./File:Berlin_by_Senitnel-2.jpg\" class=\"mw-file-description\" data-file-width=\"5875\" data-file-height=\"4414\" data-file-type=\"bitmap\" height=\"188\" width=\"250\" class=\"mw-file-element\" id=\"mwAms\"/></a><figcaption id=\"mwAmw\">Satellite image of Berlin</figcaption></figure>\n<figure class=\"mw-default-size\" typeof=\"mw:File/Thumb\" id=\"mwAm0\"><a href=\"./File:Luftbild_bln-schmoeckwitz.jpg\" class=\"mw-file-description\" id=\"mwAm4\"><img src=\"//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/aa/Luftbild_bln-schmoeckwitz.jpg/250px-Luftbild_bln-schmoeckwitz.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail\" 2x\" data-file-width=\"1280\" data-file-height=\"760\" data-file-type=\"bitmap\" height=\"148\" width=\"250\" class=\"mw-file-element\" id=\"mwAm8\"/></a><figcaption id=\"mwAnA\">The outskirts of Berlin are covered with woodlands and numerous lakes.</figcaption></figure>\n<p id=\"mwAnE\">Berlin is in northeastern Germany, in an area of low-lying marshy woodlands with a mainly flat <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Topography\" title=\"Topography\" id=\"mwAnI\">topography</a>, part of the vast <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Northern_European_Plain\" title=\"Northern European Plain\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwAnM\">Northern European Plain</a> which stretches all the way from northern France to western Russia. The <i id=\"mwAnQ\">Berliner <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Urstromtal\" title=\"Urstromtal\" id=\"mwAnU\">Urstromtal</a></i> (an ice age <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Glacial_valley\" title=\"Glacial valley\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwAnY\">glacial valley</a>), between the low <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Barnim_Plateau\" title=\"Barnim Plateau\" id=\"mwAnc\">Barnim Plateau</a> to the north and the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Teltow_plateau\" title=\"Teltow plateau\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwAng\">Teltow plateau</a> to the south, was formed by meltwater flowing from ice sheets at the end of the last <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Weichselian_glaciation\" title=\"Weichselian glaciation\" id=\"mwAnk\">Weichselian glaciation</a>. The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Spree_(river)\" title=\"Spree (river)\" id=\"mwAno\">Spree</a> follows this valley now. In Spandau, a borough in the west of Berlin, the Spree empties into the river <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Havel\" title=\"Havel\" id=\"mwAns\">Havel</a>, which flows from north to south through western Berlin. The course of the Havel is more like a chain of lakes, the largest being the Tegeler See and the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Großer_Wannsee\" title=\"Großer Wannsee\" id=\"mwAnw\">Großer Wannsee</a>. A series of lakes also feeds into the upper Spree, which flows through the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Müggelsee\" title=\"Müggelsee\" id=\"mwAn0\">Großer Müggelsee</a> in eastern Berlin.<sup about=\"#mwt265\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-68\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-68\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-68\" id=\"mwAn4\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwAn8\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAoA\">[</span>67<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwAoE\">]</span></span></a></sup></p>\n\n<p id=\"mwAoI\">Substantial parts of present-day Berlin extend onto the low plateaus on both sides of the Spree Valley. Large parts of the boroughs <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Reinickendorf\" title=\"Reinickendorf\" id=\"mwAoM\">Reinickendorf</a> and <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Pankow\" title=\"Pankow\" id=\"mwAoQ\">Pankow</a> lie on the Barnim Plateau, while most of the boroughs of <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf\" title=\"Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf\" id=\"mwAoU\">Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Steglitz-Zehlendorf\" title=\"Steglitz-Zehlendorf\" id=\"mwAoY\">Steglitz-Zehlendorf</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Tempelhof-Schöneberg\" title=\"Tempelhof-Schöneberg\" id=\"mwAoc\">Tempelhof-Schöneberg</a>, and <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Neukölln\" title=\"Neukölln\" id=\"mwAog\">Neukölln</a> lie on the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Teltow_(region)\" title=\"Teltow (region)\" id=\"mwAok\">Teltow Plateau</a>.</p>\n\n<p id=\"mwAoo\">The borough of Spandau lies partly within the Berlin Glacial Valley and partly on the Nauen Plain, which stretches to the west of Berlin. Since 2015, the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Arkenberge\" title=\"Arkenberge\" id=\"mwAos\">Arkenberge</a> hills in Pankow at <span about=\"#mwt266\" typeof=\"mw:Transclusion\" id=\"mwAow\" data-mw='{\"parts\":[{\"template\":{\"target\":{\"wt\":\"convert\",\"href\":\"./Template:Convert\"},\"params\":{\"1\":{\"wt\":\"122\"},\"2\":{\"wt\":\"m\"},\"sp\":{\"wt\":\"us\"}},\"i\":0}}]}'>122 meters (400</span><span typeof=\"mw:Entity\" about=\"#mwt266\"> </span><span about=\"#mwt266\">ft)</span> elevation, have been the highest point in Berlin. Through the disposal of construction debris they surpassed <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Teufelsberg\" title=\"Teufelsberg\" id=\"mwAo0\">Teufelsberg</a> (<span about=\"#mwt267\" typeof=\"mw:Transclusion\" id=\"mwAo4\" data-mw='{\"parts\":[{\"template\":{\"target\":{\"wt\":\"cvt\",\"href\":\"./Template:Cvt\"},\"params\":{\"1\":{\"wt\":\"120.1\"},\"2\":{\"wt\":\"m\"},\"disp\":{\"wt\":\"or\"}},\"i\":0}}]}'>120.1</span><span typeof=\"mw:Entity\" about=\"#mwt267\"> </span><span about=\"#mwt267\">m or 394</span><span typeof=\"mw:Entity\" about=\"#mwt267\"> </span><span about=\"#mwt267\">ft</span>), which itself was made up of rubble from the ruins of the Second World War.<sup about=\"#mwt272\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-69\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-69\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-69\" id=\"mwAo8\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwApA\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwApE\">[</span>68<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwApI\">]</span></span></a></sup> The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Müggelberge\" title=\"Müggelberge\" id=\"mwApM\">Müggelberge</a> at <span about=\"#mwt268\" typeof=\"mw:Transclusion\" id=\"mwApQ\"
