2x\" data-file-width=\"5080\" data-file-height=\"2540\" data-file-type=\"bitmap\" height=\"125\" width=\"250\" class=\"mw-file-element\" id=\"mwCLQ\"/></a><figcaption id=\"mwCLU\">The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Humboldt_University_of_Berlin\" title=\"Humboldt University of Berlin\" id=\"mwCLY\">Humboldt University of Berlin</a>, the world's first modern university,<sup about=\"#mwt787\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-202\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-202\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-202\" id=\"mwCLc\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCLg\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCLk\">[</span>201<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCLo\">]</span></span></a></sup> is affiliated with 57 Nobel Prize winners.</figcaption></figure>\n\n<p id=\"mwCLs\"><span about=\"#mwt788\" typeof=\"mw:Transclusion\" id=\"mwCLw\" data-mw='{\"parts\":[{\"template\":{\"target\":{\"wt\":\"as of\",\"href\":\"./Template:As_of\"},\"params\":{\"1\":{\"wt\":\"2014\"}},\"i\":0}}]}'>As of 2014</span><sup class=\"plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update\" style=\"display:none;\" about=\"#mwt788\"><a rel=\"mw:ExtLink\" href=\"https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Berlin&amp;action=edit\" class=\"external text\" data-mw-original-href=\"//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Berlin&amp;action=edit\"><span typeof=\"mw:Entity\">[</span>update<span typeof=\"mw:Entity\">]</span></a></sup><span typeof=\"mw:Nowiki\" about=\"#mwt788\"></span><link rel=\"mw:PageProp/Category\" href=\"./Category:Articles_containing_potentially_dated_statements_from_2014\" about=\"#mwt788\"/><link rel=\"mw:PageProp/Category\" href=\"./Category:All_articles_containing_potentially_dated_statements\" about=\"#mwt788\" id=\"mwCL0\"/>, Berlin had 878 schools, teaching 340,658 students in 13,727 classes and 56,787 trainees in businesses and elsewhere.<sup about=\"#mwt792\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-berlin.de_142-2\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{\"name\":\"berlin.de\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-berlin.de-142\" id=\"mwCL4\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCL8\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCMA\">[</span>141<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCME\">]</span></span></a></sup> The city has a 6-year primary education program. After completing primary school, students continue to the <span title=\"German-language text\" about=\"#mwt789\" typeof=\"mw:Transclusion\" id=\"mwCMI\" data-mw='{\"parts\":[{\"template\":{\"target\":{\"wt\":\"lang\",\"href\":\"./Template:Lang\"},\"params\":{\"1\":{\"wt\":\"de\"},\"2\":{\"wt\":\"Sekundarschule\"}},\"i\":0}}]}'><i lang=\"de\">Sekundarschule</i></span><link rel=\"mw:PageProp/Category\" href=\"./Category:Articles_containing_German-language_text\" about=\"#mwt789\" id=\"mwCMM\"/> (a comprehensive school) or <span title=\"German-language text\" about=\"#mwt790\" typeof=\"mw:Transclusion\" id=\"mwCMQ\" data-mw='{\"parts\":[{\"template\":{\"target\":{\"wt\":\"lang\",\"href\":\"./Template:Lang\"},\"params\":{\"1\":{\"wt\":\"de\"},\"2\":{\"wt\":\"Gymnasium\"}},\"i\":0}}]}'><i lang=\"de\">Gymnasium</i></span><link rel=\"mw:PageProp/Category\" href=\"./Category:Articles_containing_German-language_text\" about=\"#mwt790\" id=\"mwCMU\"/> (college preparatory school). Berlin has a special bilingual school program in the <span title=\"German-language text\" about=\"#mwt791\" typeof=\"mw:Transclusion\" id=\"mwCMY\" data-mw='{\"parts\":[{\"template\":{\"target\":{\"wt\":\"lang\",\"href\":\"./Template:Lang\"},\"params\":{\"1\":{\"wt\":\"de\"},\"2\":{\"wt\":\"Europaschule\"}},\"i\":0}}]}'><i lang=\"de\">Europaschule</i></span><link rel=\"mw:PageProp/Category\" href=\"./Category:Articles_containing_German-language_text\" about=\"#mwt791\" id=\"mwCMc\"/>, in which children are taught the curriculum in German and a foreign language, starting in primary school and continuing in high school.<sup about=\"#mwt795\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-203\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-203\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-203\" id=\"mwCMg\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCMk\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCMo\">[</span>202<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCMs\">]</span></span></a></sup></p>\n\n<p id=\"mwCMw\">The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Französisches_Gymnasium_Berlin\" title=\"Französisches Gymnasium Berlin\" id=\"mwCM0\">Französisches Gymnasium Berlin</a>, which was founded in 1689 to teach the children of Huguenot refugees, offers (German/French) instruction.<sup about=\"#mwt799\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-204\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-204\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-204\" id=\"mwCM4\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCM8\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCNA\">[</span>203<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCNE\">]</span></span></a></sup> The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./John_F._Kennedy_School,_Berlin\" title=\"John F. Kennedy School, Berlin\" id=\"mwCNI\">John F. Kennedy School</a>, a bilingual German–American public school in <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Zehlendorf_(Berlin)\" title=\"Zehlendorf (Berlin)\" id=\"mwCNM\">Zehlendorf</a>, is particularly popular with children of diplomats and the English-speaking expatriate community. 82 <span title=\"German-language text\" about=\"#mwt796\" typeof=\"mw:Transclusion\" id=\"mwCNQ\" capital region is one of the most prolific centers of higher education and research in Germany and Europe. Historically, 67 Nobel Prize winners are affiliated with the Berlin-based universities.</p>\n\n<p id=\"mwCOk\">The city has four public research universities and more than 30 private, professional, and technical colleges <i id=\"mwCOo\">(Hochschulen)</i>, offering a wide range of disciplines.<sup about=\"#mwt810\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-207\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-207\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-207\" id=\"mwCOs\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCOw\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCO0\">[</span>206<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCO4\">]</span></span></a></sup> A record number of 175,651 students were enrolled in the winter term of 2015/16.<sup about=\"#mwt813\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-208\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-208\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-208\" id=\"mwCO8\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCPA\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCPE\">[</span>207<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCPI\">]</span></span></a></sup> Among them around 18% have an international background.</p>\n\n<p id=\"mwCPM\">The three largest universities combined have approximately 103,000 enrolled students. There are the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Free_University_of_Berlin\" title=\"Free University of Berlin\" id=\"mwCPQ\">Freie Universität Berlin</a> <i id=\"mwCPU\">(Free University of Berlin, FU Berlin)</i> with about 33,000<sup about=\"#mwt816\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-209\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-209\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-209\" id=\"mwCPY\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCPc\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCPg\">[</span>208<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCPk\">]</span></span></a></sup> students, the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Humboldt_University_of_Berlin\" title=\"Humboldt University of Berlin\" id=\"mwCPo\">Humboldt Universität zu Berlin</a> <i id=\"mwCPs\">(HU Berlin)</i> with 35,000<sup about=\"#mwt819\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-210\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-210\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-210\" id=\"mwCPw\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCP0\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCP4\">[</span>209<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCP8\">]</span></span></a></sup> students, and <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Technische_Universität_Berlin\" title=\"Technische Universität Berlin\" id=\"mwCQA\">Technische Universität Berlin</a> <i id=\"mwCQE\">(TU Berlin)</i> with 35,000<sup about=\"#mwt822\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-211\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-211\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-211\" id=\"mwCQI\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCQM\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCQQ\">[</span>210<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCQU\">]</span></span></a></sup> students. The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Charité\" title=\"Charité\" id=\"mwCQY\">Charité</a> Medical School has around 8,000 students.<sup about=\"#mwt823\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-Charité_–_Universitätsmedizin_Berlin_201-1\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{\"name\":\"Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-Charité_–_Universitätsmedizin_Berlin-201\" id=\"mwCQc\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCQg\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCQk\">[</span>200<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCQo\">]</span></span></a></sup> The FU, the HU, the TU, and the Charité make up the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berlin_University_Alliance\" title=\"Berlin University Alliance\" id=\"mwCQs\">Berlin University Alliance</a>, which has received funding from the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./German_Universities_Excellence_Initiative\" title=\"German Universities Excellence Initiative\" id=\"mwCQw\">Excellence Strategy</a> program of the German government.<sup about=\"#mwt826\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-212\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-212\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-212\" id=\"mwCQ0\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCQ4\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCQ8\">[</span>211<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCRA\">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about=\"#mwt829\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-213\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-213\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-213\" id=\"mwCRE\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCRI\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCRM\">[</span>212<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCRQ\">]</span></span></a></sup> The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berlin_University_of_the_Arts\" title=\"Berlin University of the Arts\" id=\"mwCRU\">Universität der Künste</a> <i id=\"mwCRY\">(UdK)</i> has about 4,000 students and <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./ESMT_Berlin\" title=\"ESMT Berlin\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCRc\">ESMT Berlin</a> is only one of four business schools in Germany with <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Triple_accreditation\" title=\"Triple accreditation\" id=\"mwCRg\">triple accreditation</a>.<sup about=\"#mwt832\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-214\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-214\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-214\" rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Hertie_School\" title=\"Hertie School\" id=\"mwCR0\">Hertie School</a>, a private public policy school located in Mitte, has more than 900 students and doctoral students. 11,000 students, the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berliner_Hochschule_für_Technik\" title=\"Berliner Hochschule für Technik\" id=\"mwCR8\">Berlin University of Applied Sciences and Technology</a> of about 12,000 students, and the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./HTW_Berlin\" title=\"HTW Berlin\" id=\"mwCSA\">Hochschule für Technik und Wirtschaft</a> (University of Applied Sciences for Engineering and Economics) of about 14,000 students.</p>\n\n</section><section data-mw-section-id=\"43\" id=\"mwCSE\"><h3 id=\"Research\">Research</h3>\n<figure class=\"mw-default-size\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCSc\">Adlershof</a></figcaption></figure>\n\n<p id=\"mwCSg\">The city has a high density of internationally renowned research institutions, such as the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Fraunhofer_Society\" title=\"Fraunhofer Society\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCSk\">Fraunhofer Society</a>, the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./DLR_Institute_for_Planetary_Research\" title=\"DLR Institute for Planetary Research\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCSo\">DLR Institute for Planetary Research</a>, the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Leibniz_Association\" title=\"Leibniz Association\" id=\"mwCSs\">Leibniz Association</a>, the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Helmholtz_Association_of_German_Research_Centres\" title=\"Helmholtz Association of German Research Centres\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCSw\">Helmholtz Association</a>, and the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Max_Planck_Society\" title=\"Max Planck Society\" id=\"mwCS0\">Max Planck Society</a>, which are independent of, or only loosely connected to its universities.<sup about=\"#mwt835\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-215\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-215\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-215\" id=\"mwCS4\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCS8\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCTA\">[</span>214<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCTE\">]</span></span></a></sup> In 2012, around 65,000 professional scientists were working in <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Research_and_development\" title=\"Research and development\" id=\"mwCTI\">research and development</a> in the city.<sup about=\"#mwt836\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-berlin.de_142-3\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{\"name\":\"berlin.de\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-berlin.de-142\" id=\"mwCTM\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCTQ\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCTU\">[</span>141<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCTY\">]</span></span></a></sup></p>\n\n<p id=\"mwCTc\">Berlin is one of the knowledge and innovation communities (KIC) of the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./European_Institute_of_Innovation_and_Technology\" title=\"European Institute of Innovation and Technology\" id=\"mwCTg\">European Institute of Innovation and Technology</a> (EIT).<sup about=\"#mwt839\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-216\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-216\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-216\" id=\"mwCTk\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCTo\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCTs\">[</span>215<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCTw\">]</span></span></a></sup> The KIC is based at the Center for Entrepreneurship at TU Berlin and has a focus in the development of IT industries. It partners with major multinational companies such as <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Siemens\" title=\"Siemens\" id=\"mwCT0\">Siemens</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Deutsche_Telekom\" title=\"Deutsche Telekom\" id=\"mwCT4\">Deutsche Telekom</a>, and <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./SAP_SE\" title=\"SAP SE\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCT8\">SAP</a>.<sup about=\"#mwt842\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-217\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-217\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-217\" id=\"mwCUA\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCUE\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCUI\">[</span>216<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCUM\">]</span></span></a></sup></p>\n\n<p id=\"mwCUQ\">One of Europe's successful research, business and technology <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./List_of_technology_centers\" title=\"List of technology centers\" id=\"mwCUU\">clusters</a> is based at <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./WISTA\" title=\"WISTA\" id=\"mwCUY\">WISTA</a> in <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berlin-Adlershof\" title=\"Berlin-Adlershof\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCUc\">Berlin-Adlershof</a>, with more than 1,000 affiliated firms, university departments and scientific institutions.<sup about=\"#mwt845\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-218\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-218\"}}'><a id=\"mwCUs\">]</span></span></a></sup></p>\n\n<p id=\"mwCUw\">In addition to the university-affiliated libraries, the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Staatsbibliothek_zu_Berlin\" title=\"Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCU0\">Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin</a> is a major research library. Its two main locations are on Potsdamer Straße and on <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Unter_den_Linden\" title=\"Unter den Linden\" id=\"mwCU4\">Unter den Linden</a>. There are also 86 public libraries in the city.<sup about=\"#mwt846\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-berlin.de_142-4\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{\"name\":\"berlin.de\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-berlin.de-142\" id=\"mwCU8\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCVA\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCVE\">[</span>141<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCVI\">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./ResearchGate\" title=\"ResearchGate\" id=\"mwCVM\">ResearchGate</a>, a global social networking site for scientists, is based in Berlin.</p>\n\n</section></section><section data-mw-section-id=\"44\" id=\"mwCVQ\"><h2 id=\"Culture\">Culture</h2>\n<span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCWQ\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCWU\">[</span>218<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCWY\">]</span></span></a></sup> The diversity and vivacity of the data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-220\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-220\" id=\"mwCWc\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCWg\"><span id=\"mwCWs\">Young people, international artists and entrepreneurs continued to settle in the city and made Berlin a popular entertainment center in the world.<sup about=\"#mwt858\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-221\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-221\"}}'><a href=\"./Universal_Music_Group\" title=\"Universal Music Group\" id=\"mwCXE\">Universal Music Group</a> who decided to move their headquarters to the banks of the River Spree.<sup about=\"#mwt861\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-222\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-222\"}}'><a href=\"./Category:All_articles_containing_potentially_dated_statements\" about=\"#mwt870\" id=\"mwCY0\"/> Berlin is home to 138 museums and more than 400 art galleries.<sup about=\"#mwt871\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-berlin.de_142-5\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{\"name\":\"berlin.de\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-berlin.de-142\" id=\"mwCY4\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCY8\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCZA\">[</span>141<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCZE\">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about=\"#mwt874\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-225\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-225\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-225\" id=\"mwCZI\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCZM\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCZQ\">[</span>224<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCZU\">]</span></span></a></sup> The ensemble on the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Museum_Island\" title=\"Museum Island\" id=\"mwCZY\">Museum Island</a> is a UNESCO <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./World_Heritage_Site\" title=\"World Heritage Site\" id=\"mwCZc\">World Heritage Site</a> and is in the northern part of the Spree Island between the Spree and the Kupfergraben.<sup about=\"#mwt875\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-UNESCO_18-2\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{\"name\":\"UNESCO\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-UNESCO-18\" id=\"mwCZg\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCZk\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCZo\">[</span>17<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCZs\">]</span></span></a></sup> As early as 1841 it was designated a \"district dedicated to art and antiquities\" by a royal decree. Subsequently, the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Altes_Museum\" title=\"Altes Museum\" id=\"mwCZw\">Altes Museum</a> was built in the Lustgarten. The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Neues_Museum\" title=\"Neues Museum\" id=\"mwCZ0\">Neues Museum</a>, which displays the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Nefertiti_Bust\" title=\"Nefertiti Bust\" id=\"mwCZ4\">bust of Queen Nefertiti</a>,<sup about=\"#mwt878\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-226\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-226\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-226\" id=\"mwCZ8\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCaA\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCaE\">[</span>225<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCaI\">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Alte_Nationalgalerie\" title=\"Alte Nationalgalerie\" id=\"mwCaM\">Alte Nationalgalerie</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Pergamon_Museum\" title=\"Pergamon Museum\" id=\"mwCaQ\">Pergamon Museum</a>, and <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Bode_Museum\" title=\"Bode Museum\" id=\"mwCaU\">Bode Museum</a> were built there.</p>\n\n<p id=\"mwCaY\">Apart from the Museum Island, there are many additional museums in the city. The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Gemäldegalerie,_Berlin\" title=\"Gemäldegalerie, Berlin\" id=\"mwCac\">Gemäldegalerie</a> (Painting Gallery) focuses on the paintings of the \"old masters\" from the 13th to the 18th centuries, while the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Neue_Nationalgalerie\" title=\"Neue Nationalgalerie\" id=\"mwCag\">Neue Nationalgalerie</a> (New National Gallery, built by <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Ludwig_Mies_van_der_Rohe\" title=\"Ludwig Mies van der Rohe\" id=\"mwCak\">Ludwig Mies van der Rohe</a>) specializes in 20th-century European painting. The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Hamburger_Bahnhof\" title=\"Hamburger Bahnhof\" id=\"mwCao\">Hamburger Bahnhof</a>, in <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Moabit\" title=\"Moabit\" id=\"mwCas\">Moabit</a>, exhibits a major collection of modern and contemporary art. The expanded <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Deutsches_Historisches_Museum\" title=\"Deutsches Historisches Museum\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCaw\">Deutsches Historisches Museum</a> reopened in the Zeughaus with an overview of German history spanning more than a millennium. The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Bauhaus_Archive\" title=\"Bauhaus Archive\" id=\"mwCa0\">Bauhaus Archive</a> is a museum of 20th-century design from the famous <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Bauhaus\" title=\"Bauhaus\" id=\"mwCa4\">Bauhaus</a> school. <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Museum_Berggruen\" title=\"Museum Berggruen\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCa8\">Museum Berggruen</a> houses the collection of noted 20th century collector <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Heinz_Berggruen\" title=\"Heinz Berggruen\" id=\"mwCbA\">Heinz Berggruen</a>, and features an extensive assortment of works by <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Picasso\" title=\"Picasso\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCbE\">Picasso</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Matisse\" title=\"Matisse\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCbI\">Matisse</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Cézanne\" title=\"Cézanne\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCbM\">Cézanne</a>, and <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Giacometti\" title=\"Giacometti\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCbQ\">Giacometti</a>, among others.<sup about=\"#mwt881\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-227\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-227\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-227\" id=\"mwCbU\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCbY\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCbc\">[</span>226<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCbg\">]</span></span></a></sup> The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Kupferstichkabinett_Berlin\" title=\"Kupferstichkabinett Berlin\" id=\"mwCbk\">Kupferstichkabinett</a> Berlin (Museum of Prints and Drawings) is part of the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berlin_State_Museums\" title=\"Berlin State Museums\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCbo\">Staatlichen Museen zu Berlin</a> (Berlin State Museums) and the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Kulturforum\" title=\"Kulturforum\" id=\"mwCbs\">Kulturforum at Potsdamer Platz</a> in the Tiergarten district of Berlin's Mitte district. It is the largest museum of the graphic arts in Germany and at the same time one of the four most important collections of its kind in the world.<sup about=\"#mwt884\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-228\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-228\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-228\" id=\"mwCbw\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCb0\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCb4\">[</span>227<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCb8\">]</span></span></a></sup> The collection includes <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Friedrich_Gilly\" title=\"Friedrich Gilly\" id=\"mwCcA\">Friedrich Gilly</a>'s design for the monument to Frederick II of Prussia.<sup about=\"#mwt887\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-229\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-229\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-229\" id=\"mwCcE\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCcI\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCcM\">[</span>228<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCcQ\">]</span></span></a></sup></p>\n<figure class=\"mw-default-size\" typeof=\"mw:File/Thumb\" id=\"mwCcU\"><a href=\"./File:Exterior_of_Fotografiska_Berlin.jpg\" class=\"mw-file-description\" id=\"mwCcY\"><img resource=\"./File:Exterior_of_Fotografiska_Berlin.jpg\" src=\"//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b1/Exterior_of_Fotografiska_Berlin.jpg/250px-Exterior_of_Fotografiska_Berlin.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail\" decoding=\"async\" loading=\"lazy\" srcset=\"//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b1/Exterior_of_Fotografiska_Berlin.jpg/500px-Exterior_of_Fotografiska_Berlin.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x\" alt=\"Exterior of Fotografiska Berlin\" data-file-width=\"6496\" data-file-height=\"4331\" data-file-type=\"bitmap\" height=\"167\" width=\"250\" class=\"mw-file-element\" id=\"mwCcc\"/></a><figcaption id=\"mwCcg\">Exterior of <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Fotografiska\" title=\"Fotografiska\" id=\"mwCck\">Fotografiska Berlin</a> on Oranienburger Str.</figcaption></figure>\n<p id=\"mwCco\">Berlin hosts several major institutions dedicated to photography, reflecting the city's historical and contemporary engagement with the medium. The Museum für Fotografie, part of the Staatliche Museen zu Berlin and home to the Helmut Newton Foundation, presents historical and contemporary photographic works alongside the permanent exhibition <i id=\"mwCcs\">Helmut Newton's Private Property</i>. <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Fotografiska\" title=\"Fotografiska\" id=\"mwCcw\">Fotografiska</a> Berlin, opened in 2023 in the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Kunsthaus_Tacheles\" title=\"Kunsthaus Tacheles\" id=\"mwCc0\">Kunsthaus Tacheles</a>, focuses on modern and contemporary photography through showcasing local and international photographers alongside public programming. <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./C/O_Berlin\" title=\"C/O Berlin\" id=\"mwCc4\">C/O Berlin</a>, located in the Amerika Haus near <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Zoologischer_Garten_Berlin\" title=\"Zoologischer Garten Berlin\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCc8\">Zoologischer Garten</a>, is a leading exhibition space for photography and visual media, known for showcasing both established and emerging photographers. Photography also plays a significant role within broader institutions such as the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berlinische_Galerie\" title=\"Berlinische Galerie\" id=\"mwCdA\">Berlinische Galerie</a>, which integrates photography into its presentation of modern art, and the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Kunstbibliothek_Berlin\" title=\"Kunstbibliothek Berlin\" id=\"mwCdE\">Kunstbibliothek Berlin</a>, which holds an extensive photographic archive. Additional venues such as the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Friedrichshain_Photo_Gallery\" title=\"Friedrichshain Photo Gallery\" id=\"mwCdI\">Friedrichshain Photo Gallery</a> contribute to the city's documentary and socially engaged photographic culture.</p>\n\n<figure class=\"mw-default-size mw-halign-right\" typeof=\"mw:File/Thumb\" id=\"mwCdM\"><a href=\"./File:Ishtar_Gate_at_Berlin_Museum.jpg\" class=\"mw-file-description\" id=\"mwCdQ\"><img resource=\"./File:Ishtar_Gate_at_Berlin_Museum.jpg\" src=\"//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e3/Ishtar_Gate_at_Berlin_Museum.jpg/250px-Ishtar_Gate_at_Berlin_Museum.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail\" decoding=\"async\" loading=\"lazy\" srcset=\"//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e3/Ishtar_Gate_at_Berlin_Museum.jpg/500px-Ishtar_Gate_at_Berlin_Museum.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x\" data-file-width=\"1024\" data-file-height=\"768\" data-file-type=\"bitmap\" height=\"188\" width=\"250\" class=\"mw-file-element\" id=\"mwCdU\"/></a><figcaption id=\"mwCdY\">The reconstructed <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Ishtar_Gate\" title=\"Ishtar Gate\" id=\"mwCdc\">Ishtar Gate</a> of Babylon at the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Pergamon_Museum\" title=\"Pergamon Museum\" id=\"mwCdg\">Pergamon Museum</a></figcaption></figure>\n<figure class=\"mw-default-size mw-halign-right\" typeof=\"mw:File/Thumb\" id=\"mwCdk\"><a href=\"./File:JewishMuseumBerlin.jpg\" class=\"mw-file-description\" id=\"mwCdo\"><img resource=\"./File:JewishMuseumBerlin.jpg\" src=\"//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dd/JewishMuseumBerlin.jpg/250px-JewishMuseumBerlin.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail\" decoding=\"async\" loading=\"lazy\" srcset=\"//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dd/JewishMuseumBerlin.jpg/500px-JewishMuseumBerlin.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&amp;utm_campaign=parser&amp;utm_content=thumbnail 2x\" data-file-width=\"770\" data-file-height=\"597\" data-file-type=\"bitmap\" height=\"194\" width=\"250\" class=\"mw-file-element\" id=\"mwCds\"/></a><figcaption id=\"mwCdw\">The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Jewish_Museum_Berlin\" title=\"Jewish Museum Berlin\" id=\"mwCd0\">Jewish Museum</a> presents two millennia of <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./German_Jews\" title=\"German Jews\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCd4\">German–Jewish history</a>.</figcaption></figure>\n\n<p id=\"mwCd8\">The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Jewish_Museum_Berlin\" title=\"Jewish Museum Berlin\" id=\"mwCeA\">Jewish Museum</a> has a standing exhibition on two millennia of German-Jewish history.<sup about=\"#mwt890\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-230\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-230\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-230\" id=\"mwCeE\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCeI\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCeM\">[</span>229<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCeQ\">]</span></span></a></sup> The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./German_Museum_of_Technology_(Berlin)\" title=\"German Museum of Technology (Berlin)\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCeU\">German Museum of Technology</a> in <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Kreuzberg\" title=\"Kreuzberg\" id=\"mwCeY\">Kreuzberg</a> has a large collection of historical technical artifacts. The <i id=\"mwCec\"><a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Natural_History_Museum,_Berlin\" title=\"Natural History Museum, Berlin\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCeg\">Museum für Naturkunde</a></i> (Berlin's <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Natural_history_museum\" title=\"Natural history museum\" id=\"mwCek\">natural history museum</a>) exhibits <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Natural_history\" title=\"Natural history\" id=\"mwCeo\">natural history</a> near <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berlin_Hauptbahnhof\" title=\"Berlin Hauptbahnhof\" id=\"mwCes\">Berlin Hauptbahnhof</a>. It has the largest mounted dinosaur in the world (a <i id=\"mwCew\"><a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Giraffatitan\" title=\"Giraffatitan\" id=\"mwCe0\">Giraffatitan</a></i> skeleton). A well-preserved specimen of <i id=\"mwCe4\"><a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Tyrannosaurus\" title=\"Tyrannosaurus\" id=\"mwCe8\">Tyrannosaurus rex</a></i> and the early bird <i id=\"mwCfA\"><a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Archaeopteryx\" title=\"Archaeopteryx\" id=\"mwCfE\">Archaeopteryx</a></i> are at display as well.<sup about=\"#mwt893\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-231\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-231\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-231\" id=\"mwCfI\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCfM\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCfQ\">[</span>230<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCfU\">]</span></span></a></sup></p>\n\n<p id=\"mwCfY\">In <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Dahlem_(Berlin)\" title=\"Dahlem (Berlin)\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCfc\">Dahlem</a>, there are several museums of world art and culture, such as the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Museum_of_Asian_Art\" title=\"Museum of Asian Art\" id=\"mwCfg\">Museum of Asian Art</a>, the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Ethnological_Museum_of_Berlin\" title=\"Ethnological Museum of Berlin\" id=\"mwCfk\">Ethnological Museum</a>, the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Museum_Europäischer_Kulturen\" title=\"Museum Europäischer Kulturen\" id=\"mwCfo\">Museum of European Cultures</a>, as well as the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Allied_Museum\" title=\"Allied Museum\" id=\"mwCfs\">Allied Museum</a>. The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Brücke_Museum\" title=\"Brücke Museum\" id=\"mwCfw\">Brücke Museum</a> features one of the largest collection of works by artist of the early 20th-century expressionist movement. In <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Lichtenberg,_Berlin\" title=\"Lichtenberg, Berlin\" id=\"mwCf0\">Lichtenberg</a>, on the grounds of the former <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Stasi\" title=\"Stasi\" id=\"mwCf4\">East German Ministry for State Security</a>, is the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Stasi_Museum\" title=\"Stasi Museum\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCf8\">Stasi Museum</a>. The site of <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Checkpoint_Charlie\" title=\"Checkpoint Charlie\" id=\"mwCgA\">Checkpoint Charlie</a>, one of the most renowned crossing points of the Berlin Wall, is still preserved. A private <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Checkpoint_Charlie_Museum\" title=\"Checkpoint Charlie Museum\" id=\"mwCgE\">museum venture</a> exhibits a comprehensive documentation of detailed plans and strategies devised by people who tried to flee from the East.</p>\n\n<p id=\"mwCgI\">The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Beate_Uhse_Erotic_Museum\" title=\"Beate Uhse Erotic Museum\" id=\"mwCgM\">Beate Uhse Erotic Museum</a> claimed to be the largest erotic museum in the world until it closed in 2014.<sup about=\"#mwt896\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-232\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-232\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-232\" id=\"mwCgQ\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCgU\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCgY\">[</span>231<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCgc\">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about=\"#mwt899\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-233\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-233\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-233\" id=\"mwCgg\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCgk\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCgo\">[</span>232<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCgs\">]</span></span></a></sup></p>\n\n<p id=\"mwCgw\">The cityscape of Berlin displays large quantities of urban <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Street_art\" title=\"Street art\" id=\"mwCg0\">street art</a>.<sup about=\"#mwt902\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-234\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-234\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-234\" id=\"mwCg4\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCg8\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwChA\">[</span>233<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwChE\">]</span></span></a></sup> It has become a significant part of the city's cultural heritage and has its roots in the graffiti scene of <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Kreuzberg\" title=\"Kreuzberg\" id=\"mwChI\">Kreuzberg</a> of the 1980s.<sup about=\"#mwt905\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-235\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-235\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-235\" id=\"mwChM\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwChQ\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwChU\">[</span>234<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwChY\">]</span></span></a></sup> The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berlin_Wall_graffiti_art\" title=\"Berlin Wall graffiti art\" id=\"mwChc\">Berlin Wall</a> itself has become one of the largest open-air canvasses in the world.<sup about=\"#mwt908\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-236\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-236\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-236\" id=\"mwChg\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwChk\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCho\">[</span>235<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwChs\">]</span></span></a></sup> The leftover stretch along the Spree river in <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Friedrichshain\" title=\"Friedrichshain\" id=\"mwChw\">Friedrichshain</a> remains as the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./East_Side_Gallery\" title=\"East Side Gallery\" id=\"mwCh0\">East Side Gallery</a>. Berlin today is consistently rated as an important world city for street art culture.<sup about=\"#mwt911\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-237\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-237\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-237\" id=\"mwCh4\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCh8\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCiA\">[</span>236<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCiE\">]</span></span></a></sup>\nBerlin has galleries which are quite rich in contemporary art. Located in Mitte, KW Institute for Contemporary Art, KOW, Sprüth Magers; Kreuzberg there are a few galleries as well such as Blain Southern, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Esther_Schipper\" title=\"Esther Schipper\" id=\"mwCiI\">Esther Schipper</a>, Future Gallery, König Gallerie.</p>\n\n</section><section data-mw-section-id=\"46\" id=\"mwCiM\"><h3 id=\"Nightlife_and_festivals\">Nightlife and festivals</h3>\n<p id=\"mwCiQ\">Berlin's nightlife has been celebrated as one of the most diverse and vibrant of its kind.<sup about=\"#mwt914\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-238\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-238\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-238\" id=\"mwCiU\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCiY\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCic\">[</span>237<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCig\">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about=\"#mwt917\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-239\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-239\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-239\" id=\"mwCik\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCio\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCis\">[</span>238<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCiw\">]</span></span></a></sup> In the 1970s and 80s, the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./SO36\" title=\"SO36\" id=\"mwCi0\">SO36</a> in <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Kreuzberg\" title=\"Kreuzberg\" id=\"mwCi4\">Kreuzberg</a> was a center for <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Punk_music\" title=\"Punk music\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCi8\">punk music</a> and culture. The <i id=\"mwCjA\">SOUND</i> and the <i id=\"mwCjE\">Dschungel</i> gained notoriety. Throughout the 1990s, people in their 20s from all over the world, particularly those in <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Western_Europe\" title=\"Western Europe\" id=\"mwCjI\">Western</a> and Central Europe, made Berlin's club scene a premier nightlife venue. After the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Fall_of_the_Berlin_Wall\" title=\"Fall of the Berlin Wall\" id=\"mwCjM\">fall of the Berlin Wall</a> in 1989, many historic buildings in Mitte, the former city center of East Berlin, were illegally occupied and re-built by young squatters and became a fertile ground for underground and <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Counterculture\" title=\"Counterculture\" id=\"mwCjQ\">counterculture</a> gatherings.<sup about=\"#mwt920\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-240\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-240\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-240\" id=\"mwCjU\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCjY\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCjc\">[</span>239<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCjg\">]</span></span></a></sup> The central boroughs are home to many nightclubs, including the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Tresor_(club)\" title=\"Tresor (club)\" id=\"mwCjk\">Tresor</a> and the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berghain\" title=\"Berghain\" id=\"mwCjo\">Berghain</a>. The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./KitKatClub\" title=\"KitKatClub\" id=\"mwCjs\">KitKatClub</a> and several other locations are known for their sexually uninhibited parties.</p>\n\n<p id=\"mwCjw\">Clubs are not required to close at a fixed time during the weekends, and many parties last well into the morning or even all weekend, including near <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Alexanderplatz\" title=\"Alexanderplatz\" id=\"mwCj0\">Alexanderplatz</a>. Several venues have become a popular stage for the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Neo-Burlesque\" title=\"Neo-Burlesque\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCj4\">Neo-Burlesque</a> scene.</p>\n\n<p id=\"mwCj8\">Berlin has a long history of gay culture, and is an important <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Scientific-Humanitarian_Committee\" title=\"Scientific-Humanitarian Committee\" id=\"mwCkA\">birthplace of the LGBT rights movement</a>. Same-sex bars and dance halls operated freely as early as the 1880s, and the first gay magazine, <i id=\"mwCkE\"><a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Der_Eigene\" title=\"Der Eigene\" id=\"mwCkI\">Der Eigene</a></i>, started in 1896. By the 1920s, gays and lesbians had an unprecedented visibility.<sup about=\"#mwt923\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-241\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-241\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-241\" id=\"mwCkM\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCkQ\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCkU\">[</span>240<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCkY\">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about=\"#mwt926\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-242\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-242\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-242\" id=\"mwCkc\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCkg\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCkk\">[</span>241<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCko\">]</span></span></a></sup> Today, in addition to a positive atmosphere in the wider club scene, the city again has a huge number of queer clubs and festivals. The most famous and largest are <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berlin_Pride\" title=\"Berlin Pride\" id=\"mwCks\">Berlin Pride</a>, the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Christopher_Street_Day\" title=\"Christopher Street Day\" id=\"mwCkw\">Christopher Street Day</a>,<sup about=\"#mwt929\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-243\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-243\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-243\" id=\"mwCk0\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCk4\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCk8\">[</span>242<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwClA\">]</span></span></a></sup> the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Lesbian_and_Gay_City_Festival\" title=\"Lesbian and Gay City Festival\" id=\"mwClE\">Lesbian and Gay City Festival</a> in Berlin-Schöneberg, the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Kreuzberg_Pride\" title=\"Kreuzberg Pride\" id=\"mwClI\">Kreuzberg Pride</a>.</p>\n\n<p id=\"mwClM\">The annual <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berlin_International_Film_Festival\" title=\"Berlin International Film Festival\" id=\"mwClQ\">Berlin International Film Festival</a> (Berlinale) with around 500,000 admissions is considered to be the largest publicly attended film festival in the world.<sup about=\"#mwt932\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-244\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-244\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-244\" id=\"mwClU\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwClY\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwClc\">[</span>243<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwClg\">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about=\"#mwt935\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-245\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-245\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-245\" id=\"mwClk\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwClo\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCls\">[</span>244<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwClw\">]</span></span></a></sup> The Karneval der Kulturen (<i id=\"mwCl0\">Carnival of Cultures</i>), a multi-ethnic street parade, is celebrated every <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Pentecost\" title=\"Pentecost\" id=\"mwCl4\">Pentecost</a> weekend.<sup about=\"#mwt938\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-246\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-246\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-246\" id=\"mwCl8\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCmA\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCmE\">[</span>245<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCmI\">]</span></span></a></sup> Berlin is also well known for the cultural festival <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berliner_Festspiele\" title=\"Berliner Festspiele\" id=\"mwCmM\">Berliner Festspiele</a>, which includes the jazz festival <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./JazzFest_Berlin\" title=\"JazzFest Berlin\" id=\"mwCmQ\">JazzFest Berlin</a>, and <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Young_Euro_Classic\" title=\"Young Euro Classic\" id=\"mwCmU\">Young Euro Classic</a>, the largest international festival of <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Youth_orchestra\" title=\"Youth orchestra\" id=\"mwCmY\">youth orchestras</a> in the world. Several technology and media art festivals and conferences are held in the city, including <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Transmediale\" title=\"Transmediale\" id=\"mwCmc\">Transmediale</a> and <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Chaos_Communication_Congress\" title=\"Chaos Communication Congress\" id=\"mwCmg\">Chaos Communication Congress</a>. The annual <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berlin_Festival\" title=\"Berlin Festival\" id=\"mwCmk\">Berlin Festival</a> focuses on indie rock, electronic music and synthpop and is part of the International Berlin Music Week.<sup about=\"#mwt940\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-247\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-247\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-247\" id=\"mwCmo\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCms\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCmw\">[</span>246<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCm0\">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about=\"#mwt942\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-248\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-248\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-248\" id=\"mwCm4\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCm8\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCnA\">[</span>247<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCnE\">]</span></span></a></sup> Every year Berlin hosts one of the largest New Year's Eve celebrations in the world, attended by well over a million people. The focal point is the Brandenburg Gate, where midnight fireworks are centered, but various private fireworks displays take place throughout the entire city. Partygoers in Germany often toast the New Year with a glass of <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Sekt\" title=\"Sekt\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCnI\">sparkling wine</a>.</p>\n\n<ul class=\"gallery about=\"#mwt944\" id=\"mwCow\">Main article: <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Music_in_Berlin\" title=\"Music in Berlin\">Music in Berlin</a></div>\n\n<figure class=\"mw-default-size mw-halign-right\" typeof=\"mw:File/Thumb\" id=\"mwCo0\"><a href=\"./File:Rattle_BPH-Rittershaus1-Wikipedia.jpg\" class=\"mw-file-description\" id=\"mwCo4\"><img resource=\"./File:Rattle_BPH-Rittershaus1-Wikipedia.jpg\" 2x\" data-file-width=\"512\" data-file-height=\"425\" data-file-type=\"bitmap\" height=\"208\" width=\"250\" class=\"mw-file-element\" id=\"mwCo8\"/></a><figcaption id=\"mwCpA\">Sir <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Simon_Rattle\" title=\"Simon Rattle\" id=\"mwCpE\">Simon Rattle</a> conducting the renowned <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berlin_Philharmonic\" title=\"Berlin Philharmonic\" id=\"mwCpI\">Berlin Philharmonic</a></figcaption></figure>\n\n<p id=\"mwCpM\">Berlin is home to 44 theaters and stages.<sup about=\"#mwt947\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-berlin.de_142-6\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{\"name\":\"berlin.de\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-berlin.de-142\" id=\"mwCpQ\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCpU\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCpY\">[</span>141<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCpc\">]</span></span></a></sup> The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Deutsches_Theater_(Berlin)\" title=\"Deutsches Theater (Berlin)\" id=\"mwCpg\">Deutsches Theater</a> in Mitte was built in 1849–50 and has operated almost continuously since then. The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Volksbühne\" title=\"Volksbühne\" id=\"mwCpk\">Volksbühne</a> at <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Rosa-Luxemburg-Platz\" title=\"Rosa-Luxemburg-Platz\" id=\"mwCpo\">Rosa-Luxemburg-Platz</a> was built in 1913–14, though the company had been founded in 1890. The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berliner_Ensemble\" title=\"Berliner Ensemble\" id=\"mwCps\">Berliner Ensemble</a>, famous for performing the works of <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Bertolt_Brecht\" title=\"Bertolt Brecht\" id=\"mwCpw\">Bertolt Brecht</a>, was established in 1949. The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Schaubühne\" title=\"Schaubühne\" id=\"mwCp0\">Schaubühne</a> was founded in 1962 and moved to the building of the former Universum Cinema on Kurfürstendamm in 1981. With a <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Seating_capacity\" title=\"Seating capacity\" id=\"mwCp4\">seating capacity</a> of 1,895 and a stage floor of <span about=\"#mwt946\" typeof=\"mw:Transclusion\" id=\"mwCp8\" data-mw='{\"parts\":[{\"template\":{\"target\":{\"wt\":\"convert\",\"href\":\"./Template:Convert\"},\"params\":{\"1\":{\"wt\":\"2854\"},\"2\":{\"wt\":\"m2\"},\"3\":{\"wt\":\"0\"},\"sp\":{\"wt\":\"us\"}},\"i\":0}}]}'>2,854 square meters (30,720</span><span typeof=\"mw:Entity\" about=\"#mwt946\"> </span><span about=\"#mwt946\">sq</span><span typeof=\"mw:Entity\" about=\"#mwt946\"> </span><span about=\"#mwt946\">ft)</span>, the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Friedrichstadt-Palast\" title=\"Friedrichstadt-Palast\" id=\"mwCqA\">Friedrichstadt-Palast</a> in Berlin Mitte is the largest show palace in Europe. For Berlin's independent dance and theatre scene, venues such as the Sophiensäle in Mitte and the three houses of the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Hebbel-Theater\" title=\"Hebbel-Theater\" id=\"mwCqE\">Hebbel am Ufer (HAU)</a> in Kreuzberg are important. Most productions there are also accessible to an English-speaking audience. Some of the dance and theatre groups that also work internationally (<a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Gob_Squad\" title=\"Gob Squad\" id=\"mwCqI\">Gob Squad</a>, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Rimini_Protokoll\" title=\"Rimini Protokoll\" id=\"mwCqM\">Rimini Protokoll</a>) are based there, as well as festivals such as the international festival <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Tanz_im_August\" title=\"Tanz im August\" id=\"mwCqQ\">Dance in August</a>.</p>\n\n<p id=\"mwCqU\">Berlin has three <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Opera_house\" title=\"Opera house\" id=\"mwCqY\">opera houses</a>: the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Deutsche_Oper\" title=\"Deutsche Oper\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCqc\">Deutsche Oper</a>, the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berlin_State_Opera\" title=\"Berlin State Opera\" id=\"mwCqg\">Berlin State Opera</a>, and the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Komische_Oper\" title=\"Komische Oper\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCqk\">Komische Oper</a>. The Berlin State Opera on <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Unter_den_Linden\" title=\"Unter den Linden\" id=\"mwCqo\">Unter den Linden</a> opened in 1742 and is the oldest of the three. Its musical director is <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Daniel_Barenboim\" title=\"Daniel Barenboim\" id=\"mwCqs\">Daniel Barenboim</a>. The Komische Oper has traditionally specialized in <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Operetta\" title=\"Operetta\" id=\"mwCqw\">operettas</a> and is also at Unter den Linden. The Deutsche Oper opened in 1912 in Charlottenburg.</p>\n\n<p id=\"mwCq0\">The city's main venue for musical theater performances are the Theater am Potsdamer Platz and <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Theater_des_Westens\" title=\"Theater des Westens\" id=\"mwCq4\">Theater des Westens</a> (built in 1895). Contemporary dance can be seen at the <i id=\"mwCq8\">Radialsystem V</i>. The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Tempodrom\" title=\"Tempodrom\" id=\"mwCrA\">Tempodrom</a> is host to concerts and circus-inspired entertainment. It also houses a multi-sensory spa experience. The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Admiralspalast\" title=\"Admiralspalast\" id=\"mwCrE\">Admiralspalast</a> in Mitte has a vibrant program of variety and music events.</p>\n\n<p id=\"mwCrI\">There are seven symphony orchestras in Berlin. The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berlin_Philharmonic_Orchestra\" title=\"Berlin Philharmonic Orchestra\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCrM\">Berlin Philharmonic Orchestra</a> is one of the preeminent orchestras in the world;<sup about=\"#mwt950\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-249\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-249\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-249\" id=\"mwCrQ\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCrU\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCrY\">[</span>248<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCrc\">]</span></span></a></sup> it is housed in the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berliner_Philharmonie\" title=\"Berliner Philharmonie\" id=\"mwCrg\">Berliner Philharmonie</a> near Potsdamer Platz on a street named for the orchestra's longest-serving conductor, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Herbert_von_Karajan\" title=\"Herbert von Karajan\" id=\"mwCrk\">Herbert von Karajan</a>.<sup about=\"#mwt954\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-250\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-250\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-250\" id=\"mwCro\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCrs\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCrw\">[</span>249<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCr0\">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Simon_Rattle\" title=\"Simon Rattle\" id=\"mwCr4\">Simon Rattle</a> was its principal conductor from 1999 to 2018, a position now held by <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Kirill_Petrenko\" title=\"Kirill Petrenko\" id=\"mwCr8\">Kirill Petrenko</a>. The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Konzerthausorchester_Berlin\" title=\"Konzerthausorchester Berlin\" id=\"mwCsA\">Konzerthausorchester Berlin</a> was founded in 1952 as the orchestra for East Berlin. <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Christoph_Eschenbach\" title=\"Christoph Eschenbach\" id=\"mwCsE\">Christoph Eschenbach</a> is its principal conductor. The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Haus_der_Kulturen_der_Welt\" title=\"Haus der Kulturen der Welt\" id=\"mwCsI\">Haus der Kulturen der Welt</a> presents exhibitions dealing with intercultural issues and stages world music and conferences.<sup about=\"#mwt957\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-251\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-251\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-251\" id=\"mwCsM\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCsQ\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCsU\">[</span>250<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCsY\">]</span></span></a></sup> The <i id=\"mwCsc\">Kookaburra</i> and the <i id=\"mwCsg\">Quatsch Comedy Club</i> are known for satire and comedy shows. In 2018, the <i id=\"mwCsk\"><a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./The_New_York_Times\" title=\"The New York Times\" id=\"mwCso\">New York Times</a></i> described Berlin as \"arguably the world capital of underground <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Electronic_music\" title=\"Electronic music\" id=\"mwCss\">electronic music</a>\".<sup about=\"#mwt960\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-252\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-252\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-252\" id=\"mwCsw\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCs0\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCs4\">[</span>251<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCs8\">]</span></span></a></sup></p>\n\n</section><section href=\"./German_cuisine\" title=\"German cuisine\" id=\"mwCtY\">cuisine</a> and culinary offerings of Berlin vary greatly. 23 restaurants in Berlin have been awarded one or more <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" of vegetarian<sup about=\"#mwt970\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-254\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-254\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-254\" id=\"mwCt0\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCt4\"><span One of Europe's largest <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Delicatessen\" title=\"Delicatessen\" id=\"mwCwI\">delicatessen</a> markets is found at the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./KaDeWe\" title=\"KaDeWe\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCwM\">KaDeWe</a>, and among the world's largest chocolate stores is <i id=\"mwCwQ\">Rausch</i>.<sup about=\"#mwt991\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-260\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-260\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-260\" id=\"mwCwU\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCwY\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCwc\">[</span>259<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCwg\">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about=\"#mwt994\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-261\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-261\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-261\" id=\"mwCwk\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCwo\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCws\">[</span>260<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCww\">]</span></span></a></sup></p>\n\n<p id=\"mwCw0\">Berlin is also home to a diverse gastronomy scene reflecting the immigrant history of the city. Turkish and Arab immigrants brought their culinary traditions to the city, such as the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Lahmacun\" title=\"Lahmacun\" id=\"mwCw4\">lahmacun</a> and <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Falafel\" title=\"Falafel\" id=\"mwCw8\">falafel</a>, which have become common fast food staples. The modern fast-food version of the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Doner_kebab\" title=\"Doner kebab\" id=\"mwCxA\">doner kebab</a> sandwich which <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Kadir_Nurman\" title=\"Kadir Nurman\" id=\"mwCxE\">evolved in Berlin</a> in the 1970s, has since become a favorite dish in Germany and elsewhere in the world.<sup about=\"#mwt997\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-262\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-262\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-262\" id=\"mwCxI\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCxM\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCxQ\">[</span>261<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCxU\">]</span></span></a></sup> Asian cuisine like Chinese, Vietnamese, Thai, Indian, Korean, and Japanese restaurants, as well as Spanish tapas bars, Italian, and Greek cuisine, can be found in many parts of the city.</p>\n\n</section><section data-mw-section-id=\"49\" id=\"mwCxY\"><h3 id=\"Recreation\">Recreation</h3>\n<p id=\"mwCxc\"><a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berlin_Zoological_Garden\" title=\"Berlin Zoological Garden\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCxg\">Zoologischer Garten Berlin</a>, the older of two zoos in the city, was founded in 1844. It is the most visited zoo in Europe and presents the most diverse range of species in the world.<sup about=\"#mwt1001\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-263\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-263\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-263\" id=\"mwCxk\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCxo\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCxs\">[</span>262<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCxw\">]</span></span></a></sup> It was the home of the captive-born celebrity polar bear <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Knut_(polar_bear)\" title=\"Knut (polar bear)\" id=\"mwCx0\">Knut</a>.<sup about=\"#mwt1004\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-264\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-264\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-264\" id=\"mwCx4\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCx8\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCyA\">[</span>263<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCyE\">]</span></span></a></sup> The city's other zoo, <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Tierpark_Berlin\" title=\"Tierpark Berlin\" id=\"mwCyI\">Tierpark Friedrichsfelde</a>, was founded in 1955.</p>\n\n<p id=\"mwCyM\"><a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berlin-Dahlem_Botanical_Garden_and_Botanical_Museum\" title=\"Berlin-Dahlem Botanical Garden and Botanical Museum\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCyQ\">Berlin's Botanischer Garten</a> includes the Botanic Museum Berlin. With an area of <span about=\"#mwt1005\" typeof=\"mw:Transclusion\" id=\"mwCyU\" data-mw='{\"parts\":[{\"template\":{\"target\":{\"wt\":\"convert\",\"href\":\"./Template:Convert\"},\"params\":{\"1\":{\"wt\":\"43\"},\"2\":{\"wt\":\"ha\"},\"3\":{\"wt\":\"acre\"}},\"i\":0}}]}'>43 hectares (110 acres)</span> and around 22,000 different plant species, it is one of the largest and most diverse collections of botanical life in the world. Other gardens in the city include the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Britzer_Garten\" title=\"Britzer Garten\" id=\"mwCyY\">Britzer Garten</a>, and the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Erholungspark_Marzahn\" title=\"Erholungspark Marzahn\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwCyc\">Gärten der Welt</a> (Gardens of the World) in Marzahn.<sup about=\"#mwt1008\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-265\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-265\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-265\" id=\"mwCyg\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCyk\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCyo\">[</span>264<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCys\">]</span></span></a></sup></p>\n\n<p id=\"mwCyw\">The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Tiergarten_(park)\" title=\"Tiergarten (park)\" id=\"mwCy0\">Tiergarten park</a> in Mitte, with landscape design by <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Peter_Joseph_Lenné\" title=\"Peter Joseph Lenné\" id=\"mwCy4\">Peter Joseph Lenné</a>, is one of Berlin's largest and most popular parks.<sup about=\"#mwt1011\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-266\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-266\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-266\" id=\"mwCy8\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCzA\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCzE\">[</span>265<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCzI\">]</span></span></a></sup> In Kreuzberg, the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Viktoriapark\" title=\"Viktoriapark\" id=\"mwCzM\">Viktoriapark</a> provides a viewing point over the southern part of inner-city Berlin. <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Treptower_Park\" title=\"Treptower Park\" id=\"mwCzQ\">Treptower Park</a>, beside the Spree in <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Treptow\" title=\"Treptow\" id=\"mwCzU\">Treptow</a>, features a large <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Soviet_War_Memorial_(Treptower_Park)\" title=\"Soviet War Memorial (Treptower Park)\" id=\"mwCzY\">Soviet War Memorial</a>. The Volkspark in <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Friedrichshain\" title=\"Friedrichshain\" id=\"mwCzc\">Friedrichshain</a>, which opened in 1848, is the oldest park in the city, with monuments, a summer outdoor cinema and several sports areas.<sup about=\"#mwt1014\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-267\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-267\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-267\" id=\"mwCzg\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCzk\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCzo\">[</span>266<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwCzs\">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Tempelhofer_Feld\" title=\"Tempelhofer Feld\" id=\"mwCzw\">Tempelhofer Feld</a>, the site of the former <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Berlin_Tempelhof_Airport\" title=\"Berlin Tempelhof Airport\" id=\"mwCz0\">city airport</a>, is the world's largest inner-city open space.<sup about=\"#mwt1017\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-268\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{},\"body\":{\"id\":\"mw-reference-text-cite_note-268\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-268\" id=\"mwCz4\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwCz8\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwC0A\">[</span>267<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwC0E\">]</span></span></a></sup></p>\n\n<p id=\"mwC0I\"><a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Potsdam\" title=\"Potsdam\" id=\"mwC0M\">Potsdam</a> is on the southwestern periphery of Berlin. The city was a residence of the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Prussia\" title=\"Prussia\" id=\"mwC0Q\">Prussian</a> kings and the <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./German_Emperor\" title=\"German Emperor\" id=\"mwC0U\">German Kaiser</a> until 1918. The area around Potsdam, in particular <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Sanssouci\" title=\"Sanssouci\" id=\"mwC0Y\">Sanssouci</a>, is known for a series of interconnected lakes and cultural landmarks. The <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Palaces_and_Parks_of_Potsdam_and_Berlin\" title=\"Palaces and Parks of Potsdam and Berlin\" id=\"mwC0c\">Palaces and Parks of Potsdam and Berlin</a> are the largest <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./World_Heritage_Site\" title=\"World Heritage Site\" id=\"mwC0g\">World Heritage Site</a> in Germany.<sup about=\"#mwt1018\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-UNESCO-2_219-1\" rel=\"dc:references\" typeof=\"mw:Extension/ref\" data-mw='{\"name\":\"ref\",\"attrs\":{\"name\":\"UNESCO-2\"}}'><a href=\"./Berlin#cite_note-UNESCO-2-219\" id=\"mwC0k\"><span class=\"mw-reflink-text\" id=\"mwC0o\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwC0s\">[</span>218<span class=\"cite-bracket\" id=\"mwC0w\">]</span></span></a></sup></p>\n\n<p id=\"mwC00\">Berlin is also well known for its numerous cafés, street musicians, beach bars along the Spree River, flea markets, boutique shops and <a rel=\"mw:WikiLink\" href=\"./Pop-up_store\" title=\"Pop-up store\" class=\"mw-redirect\" id=\"mwC04\">pop-up stores</a>, which provide recreation and leisure opportunities.<sup about=\"#mwt1021\" class=\"mw-ref reference\" id=\"cite_ref-269\"   "sections": [
    {
      "title": "",
      "level": 0,
      "text": "Berlin is the capital and largest city of Germany. With 3.7 million inhabitants, it has the highest population within its city limits of any city in the European Union. The city is also one of the states of Germany, being the third-smallest state in the country by area. Berlin is surrounded by the state of Brandenburg, bordering Brandenburg's capital Potsdam to the southwest. The urban area of Berlin has a population of 4.5 million, making it the second most populous in Germany after the Ruhr. The Berlin-Brandenburg capital region has around 6.2 million inhabitants and is Germany's second-largest metropolitan region after the Rhine-Ruhr region, as well as the fifth-biggest metropolitan region by GDP in the European Union. Berlin was built along the banks of the Spree river, which flows into the Havel in the western borough of Spandau. First documented in the 13th century and at the crossing of two important historic trade routes, Berlin was designated the capital of the Margraviate of Brandenburg (1417–1701), Kingdom of Prussia (1701–1918), German Empire (1871–1918), Weimar Republic (1919–1933), and Nazi Germany (1933–1945). Berlin served as a scientific, artistic, and philosophical hub during the Age of Enlightenment, Neoclassicism, and the German revolutions of 1848–1849. During the Gründerzeit, an industrialization-induced economic boom triggered a rapid population increase in Berlin. Berlin in the 1920s was the third-largest city in the world by population. After World War II and following Berlin's occupation, the city was split into West Berlin and East Berlin, divided by the Berlin Wall. East Berlin was declared the capital of East Germany, while Bonn became the West German capital. Following German reunification in 1990, Berlin once again became the capital of all of Germany. Due to its geographic location and history, Berlin has been called \"the heart of Europe\". Berlin is a global city of culture, politics, media and science. Its economy is based on high tech and the service sector, encompassing a diverse range of creative industries, startup companies, research facilities, and media corporations. Berlin serves as a continental hub for air and rail traffic and has a complex public transportation network. Tourism in Berlin makes the city a popular global destination. Berlin is home to several universities, such as the Humboldt University of Berlin, Technische Universität Berlin, the Berlin University of the Arts and the Free University of Berlin. The Berlin Zoological Garden is the most visited zoo in Europe. Babelsberg Studio is the world's first large-scale movie studio complex, and there are many films set in Berlin. Berlin is home to three UNESCO World Heritage Sites: Museum Island, the Palaces and Parks of Potsdam and Berlin, and the Berlin Modernism Housing Estates. Other landmarks include the Brandenburg Gate, the Reichstag building, Potsdamer Platz, the Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe, and the Berlin Wall Memorial. Berlin has numerous museums, galleries, and libraries. The city includes lakes in the western and southeastern boroughs, the largest of which is Müggelsee. About 1/3 of the city's area is composed of forests, parks and gardens, rivers, canals, and lakes."

    {
      "title": "Etymology",
      "level": 3,
      "text": "Berlin lies in northeastern Germany, in an area formerly settled by Slavs which thus exhibits many (Germanized) Slavic-derived placenames to this day (see below). The word Berlin also has its roots in the language of the West Slavs, and may be related to the Old Polabian stem berl-/birl- (\"swamp\"). Of Berlin's twelve boroughs, five bear a Slavic-derived name—Pankow, Steglitz-Zehlendorf, Marzahn-Hellersdorf, Treptow-Köpenick and Spandau; furthermore, across the city's 96 neighborhoods, there are 22 which bear a Slavic-rooted name—Altglienicke, Alt-Treptow, Britz, Buch, Buckow, Gatow, Karow, Kladow, Köpenick, Lankwitz, Lübars, Malchow, Marzahn, Pankow, Prenzlauer Berg, Rudow, Schmöckwitz, Spandau, Stadtrandsiedlung Malchow, Steglitz, Tegel and Zehlendorf."

    {
      "title": "Prehistory",
      "level": 3,
      "text": "The area of what is now Berlin has been settled for millennia. A deer mask, dated to 9,000 BCE, is attributed to the Maglemosian culture. Around 2,000 BCE dense human settlements along the Spree and Havel rivers gave rise to the Lusatian culture. Starting around 500 BCE Germanic tribes settled in a number of villages in the higher situated areas of today's Berlin. After the Semnones left around 200 CE, the Burgundians followed. In the 7th century Slavic tribes, the later known Hevelli and Sprevane, reached the region."
